item.title: Aaron Rodgers Released From Steelers: Breaking Down Timeline of Events, From Benching to Pat McAfee Show Appearance
item.description: Aaron Rodgers Released From Steelers: Breaking Down Timeline of Events, From Benching to Pat McAfee Show Appearance originally appeared on SportsNet Pittsburgh . Add SportsNet Pittsburgh as a Preferred Source by clicking here . It’s been quite a week for the Steelers organization, forced to release QB Aaron Rodgers, who is competing in his final season. The week started with a promise that Rodgers would remain the Steelers’ QB, despite the team being on a two-game losing streak. It ended with Rodgers ranting about coach Mike McCarthy and his release. There will be plenty to talk about at the Thanksgiving table, and there is sure to be more drama surrounding Rodgers and the Steelers to come. How did we get here? Here's a breakdown of the events that led to Rodgers’ release. Timeline of events leading to Aaron Rodgers' release from Steelers Monday, Nov. 23 Even after a blowout loss to the Bengals in Madrid was followed by an embarrassing defeat at the hands of third-string Joe Milton III and the Eagles, McCarthy addressed the media about Rodgers’ future, stating he "was still their quarterback." Tuesday, Nov. 24 Around 11 p.m. ET, the Steelers announced that Aaron Rodgers would be benched for Mason Rudolph. The statement went a step further by saying Rodgers would be inactive. https://t.co/F2qo4OawcY — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 25, 2026 Wed. Nov. 25 Hours after the news broke, Rodgers was announced as a special guest on The Pat McAfee Show. At around 1:40 p.m. ET , Rodgers went scorched earth on McCarthy. He accused McCarthy of sleeping in meetings, mistakenly ending a huddle with "Packers," and more. Rodgers also discovered he was being benched via Pat Freiermuth. "It's on me because I vouched for him and I had the hope it was going to be different. There's no way," Rodgers said. "He knows it's my last year, he knows it's his dream job, he's back in his hometown. It's going to be different. BREAKING NEWS: @AaronRodgers12 addresses being benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers #PMSLive https://t.co/6rggspWDGX — Pat McAfee (@PatMcAfeeShow) November 25, 2026 "I didn't see this happening, and I didn't want this to be the way that it ended. At this point, I'm not going back to Pittsburgh, and that ship has definitely sailed." About an hour later , Rodgers was released by the Steelers. We have released QB Aaron Rodgers. — Pittsburgh Steelers (@steelers) November 25, 2026 At 2:11 p.m. ET , former Steelers star James Harrison revealed "this is not the first time" he had heard of such accusations against McCarthy. This is not the first time I have heard of the kind of things @AaronRodgers12 is talking about on @PatMcAfeeShow — James Harrison (@jharrison9292) November 25, 2026 At 3 p.m. ET , ESPN's Brooke Pryor stated multiple league sources corroborated Aaron Rodgers' account of Mike McCarthy's actions . item.title: Timberwolves vs. Thunder: Live updates, highlights for Wednesday's game

item.title: Packers Hall of Famer calls out AJ Hawk for silence during Aaron Rodgers’ McAfee rant
item.description: There is at least one former player who is defending Mike McCarthy , after several have reportedly confirmed the scathing allegations spewed by Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday afternoon. Rodgers went scorched earth on the Steelers’ head coach after his benching, and he has been backed up by unnamed players. One former player, Green Bay Packers Hall of Famer Greg Jennings, who won a Super Bowl in Green Bay under McCarthy, said he could not confirm any of what Rodgers claimed. He did, however, call out former teammate A.J. Hawk for just sitting around and not speaking up while Rodgers was making his claims on The Pat McAfee Show . Jennings wishes that Hawk would have been asked if he ever experienced what Rodgers was claiming, but instead, he sat in the shadows, as he’s been known to do on the show. MORE: Wildest Moments from Aaron Rodgers’ explosive Pat McAfee appearance Greg Jennings Wanted AJ Hawk To Speak Up Greg Jennings takes a shot at A.J. Hawk over Aaron Rodgers’ ‘McAfee Show’ interview: "A large part of me just wanted someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, do you recall any of this stuff?" 🏈 📺 🧀 https://t.co/TDCzKtxMIn — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 25, 2026 “I actually am surprised at a lot of it because there’s a lot that was said in this interview from Aaron that I, it overlapped my time in Green Bay, and I can’t bear witness to any of it. I was listening to it, and a large part of me just wanted anybody and someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, A.J., do you recall any of this stuff?,” Jennings said. “I’m like, please, someone ask A.J., can you confirm or can you second any of this? Because I couldn’t. And I’ve been texting with other teammates. They could. Now, I’m not saying that what he’s saying is not true, because I don’t think he sits up there and just embellishes to embellish. So I do believe that there is some truth to it. And Mike is going to have to, you know, correct it in his way and address it.” MORE: Mike McCarthy ice cream sandwich assistant becomes most famous man in Pittsburgh Jennings has a point, but at the same time, Hawk is always quiet on the show, and he attempts to get involved in controversy. If drama isn’t his thing, there’s no need to throw his name in the mix. The Rodgers-McCarthy saga isn’t going anywhere anytime soon, so the Packers great will be able to share his thoughts if he decides to, but for now, he’s fine just being an observer. ESPN’s AJ Hawk, left, and Pat McAfee broadcast from the sideline during the College Football Playoff quarterfinal between the Ohio State Buckeyes and the Oregon Ducks at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, Calif. on Jan. 1, 2025. Ohio State won 41-21. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: The RUNDOWN: Everything you need to know about the Bears in Week 12 against the Lions
item.description: (Talia Sprague-Imagn Images) Shortly after the Bears finished celebrating a 21-13 win – their fifth in a row – over the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, a group of coaches hustled back to Halas Hall that night to begin working on a plan for Thanksgiving Day in Detroit. “That’s got to be your catch-up time really, because you’re three days short of your normal prep time,” offensive coordinator Press Taylor said via Zoom on Monday. The Bears’ schedule has been anything but normal through the first 11 weeks of the season. The last Sunday-to-Sunday week came in the transition from Week 5 to Week 6. The next comes in Week 13 to Week 14. “It’s a quick transition right here (to Thursday),” Taylor said. “Now you’re trying to catch up on time and make sure you’ve got everything downloaded.” Here’s everything you need to know about the Bears in Week 12, from the podium to the locker room to the injury report. 1. Running back D’Andre Swift’s fumble issues are an obvious concern, but he still has the trust of the coaching staff. Swift did not receive another carry after his third lost fumble of the season against the Saints in the fourth quarter on Sunday. He received a similar punishment in Week 4 against the New York Jets after his second fumble of the year – also in the fourth quarter. “He just needs to hold on to the ball and we’ll be fine,” coach Ben Johnson said Tuesday. Swift’s three fumbles match his career high for a season, doing so in 2023 with the Philadelphia Eagles and 2020 – his rookie season – with the Lions. After each fumble and subsequent late-game benching this year, Swift has still received the start the following week. 2. Swift’s issues on Sunday opened the door for Salvon Ahmed off the practice squad, who’s made the most of his opportunities. Ahmed’s quick burst out of the backfield was noticeable in his limited action against the Saints. Among the Bears’ running backs in Week 11, his 19-yard carry was the largest gain out of the backfield. Thursday’s game marks his third and final allowable elevation from the practice squad to the Bears’ game-day roster. He will require a spot on the 53-man roster if the Bears want to use him beyond Week 12. That seems likely at this point. “He’s a guy that’s always flashed for us,” Johnson said. “He had a great preseason. I think we have a number of guys on the practice squad that are right on the edge of being able to contribute on game day for us. They’re just looking for an opportunity. He’s taking full advantage of his right now.” Ahmed could also factor into the Bears’ special teams plans, with running back Roschon Johnson unavailable for Thursday due to an ankle injury he sustained on Sunday. 3. Quarterback Caleb Williams has a new weapon emerging in rookie receiver Zavion Thomas — and the rest of the league is starting to take notice. item.title: Texas Tech WR Micah Hudson expected to play on Thanksgiving vs. TCU
item.description: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images Texas Tech WR Micah Hudson expected to play on Thanksgiving vs. TCU appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Texas Tech football is visualizing securing a repeat of the Big 12 Conference title . Rival TCU represents the final regular season hurdle and now, TTU is welcoming back injured wide receiver Micah Hudson. The former five-star signing is officially expected to play on Thanksgiving Day , per College Football insider for On3 Pete Nakos. Surely Hudson’s presence will boost the offense, especially with Nakos revealing what’s also at stake for TTU. “A Thanksgiving night win will send the Red Raiders to their second consecutive Big 12 title game,” Nakos added. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) That means the Red Raiders can pursue a first-ever back-to-back conference championship. Plus can win over the College Football Playoff committee before locking in the 12-team field. Texas Tech exploded out of nowhere to win the Big 12 last season. Especially after so many years of watching the likes of former members Texas, Oklahoma and Texas A&M dominate the conference. Now coach Joey McGuire has turned the Red Raiders into the conference heavyweight. But Utah is putting together an undefeated season under first-year coach Morgan Scalley. The Utes enter Thanksgiving weekend as the last undefeated team left in the nation, after UCLA fell to Michigan this past Saturday. A Utah-Texas Tech showdown could be in the works down in AT&T Stadium down in Arlington, Texas on Dec. 4. Hudson heads into the TCU showdown catching 17 passes for 306 yards and scoring once. But his status isn’t the only pivotal return that occurred in Lubbock. TTU re-signed edge rusher LaDamion Guyton for one more season, who has delivered five sacks during his freshman season. item.title: Writer proposes Braves-Jazz Chisholm Jr. shortstop idea
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images Writer proposes Braves-Jazz Chisholm Jr. shortstop idea appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Should the Atlanta Braves consider pursuing Jazz Chisholm Jr. in MLB free agency? Atlanta needs a shortstop and Chisholm has experience at the position. Reports have said that Chisholm is receiving interest in free agency from multiple teams. While Chisholm is seemingly a popular free agent , it remains to be seen if the Braves have any interest in him. Max Ralph of MLB.com recently addressed the idea of Atlanta pursuing the former Miami Marlin and New York Yankee. “Maybe you could squint to see a fit with Jazz Chisholm Jr., whose defense has been superb at second base over the past two seasons. He has not played shortstop since 2021 with the Marlins, but he’s reportedly open to operating at spots beyond second base,” Ralph wrote. Ralph was discussing potential options for the Braves shortstop uncertainty. While the writer clearly wasn’t suggesting that Atlanta needs to go all in on Chisholm at shortstop, the idea in itself is intriguing. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Chisholm has been quite versatile from a defensive standpoint in his career. While he likely wouldn’t be the shortstop of the long-term future, signing him to a multi-year deal could be an option for Atlanta. Chisholm could end up switching positions in the future if another shortstop candidate emerges on the roster. At the very least, Chisholm could help out at the position in 2027. With that being said, the Braves are not always among the biggest spenders in free agency. They may not have a desire to dish out a multi-year deal. If Atlanta is going to bring in a star to play shortstop, it will likely be through trade. Nevertheless, Jazz Chisholm Jr. is a free agent Atlanta could at least think about pursuing. item.title: Vincent Kompany calls on Bayern Munich to embrace the adversity, regain momentum after big loss to LOSC Lille
item.description: (Photo by S. Stingl/FC Bayern via Getty Images) | FC Bayern via Getty Images There is not a lot of room for positivity at Bayern Munich. The lead at the top of the Bundesliga table is gone, the Champions League top 8 looks like an impossible dream following the 2-1 loss to Lille OSC, the injury list is long and will not immediately improve, and — to top it all off — there has been needless drama around Jamal Musiala’s contract situation that has damaged the club’s image in the general public. But head coach Vincent Kompany knows not only that dwelling on the negativity never helps, but also the key to bringing back the positivity. “This is about momentum and fighting,” Kompany broke it down (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). “We simply have to get back to winning ways and then build on that, winning not just once, but twice, three times, four times, and get the machine runn ing again. There are no excuses. It’s simply the reality of the situation, and we have to stick together. Sometimes you have to enjoy the fight an d face the challenge head-on.” It really is that simple: Winning is the key. Kompany and the team will throw everything they have into improvin g and bagging a victory against Hamburger SV this weekend, buoyed not by any of the events of the past week, but by the knowledge that the only way to look is forward. item.title: Astros Should Be In Trade Market for a Starter
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 22: Cristian Javier #53 of the Houston Astros pitches during the second inning against the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park on September 22, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images With the recent nine figure deals that starting pitchers have gotten in the last few days, it should not be lost on anyone that the Astros under Jim Crane have never give a free agent a nine figure contract. It also should not be lost on anyone that the Astros current options to fill out their starting rotation behind Hunter Brown all have various levels of risk. Options currently available to the #Astros on their 40-man roster for shaping their rotation: • Hunter Brown • Hayden Wesneski • Peter Lambert • Cristian Javier • Tatsuya Imai • Ethan Pecko • Ronel Blanco • Mike Burrows • Brandon Walter • Jackson Nezuh — Javier Gonzalez (@Astros_Coverage) November 22, 2026 Hayden Wesneski returned from Tommy John surgery last year and pitched very well in 11 starts. However he only threw 61 innings. Turning 29 in 10 days, he’s never thrown 90 innings in an MLB season. His durability to get through 33 starts, to maintain his production through 33 starts, and to produce as he did last season are all significant questions. Peter Lambert was a huge surprise for the team last season. At the MLB level, he set career highs in starts (29) and inning (155.2) and his 3.82 ERA is a number he had never previously approached (as evidenced by his career 5.32 ERA even after this past season). Entering his age 30 season, did the former 2nd round pick become a late bloomer or is a hard regression coming? How will his arm bounce back from a career high workload? Cristian Javier hasn’t looked the same since his phenomenal 2022 season. Since then, he has seen both a decrease and an inconsistency in velocity, he’s frequently had command issues, and he’s had Tommy John surgery. Last season wasn’t a pretty one for him, but his 1.96 ERA in September offered hope. Can Javier finally rebound at 30 years old, 5 seasons after his best work? Was September a breakthrough or an anomaly? Are his velocity issues a thing of the past? Can he rediscover his “invisiball” consistently? What is Javier at this point in his career? Tatsuya Imai’s rookie season in Houston was a major disappointment. He has shown tremendous stuff but also an incredible lack of mental fortitude. He frequently lost confidence in his stuff, and when he would lose the plate he couldn’t regain it in the same game. It happened entirely too often. His explanations through his translators of feeling isolated and struggling to adapt to the American game and lifestyle are certainly concerning. But $18M is more than even the best players in Japan make, and he opted in. His agent Scott Boras is engaging with the Astros to help Imai find his consistency. item.title: Seahawks’ Sam Darnold expected to start vs. 49ers, but there’s a catch
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Steven Bisig-Imagn Images Seahawks’ Sam Darnold expected to start vs. 49ers, but there’s a catch appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Sam Darnold could be back out there under center on Sunday, when the Seattle Seahawks go on a rematch against NFC West Division rivals San Francisco 49ers. But that still depends on how well he does in practice . “Mike Macdonald reiterates that plan is for Sam Darnold to start Sunday as long as practice today goes well,” Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times shared via a social media post on X, formerly Twitter. An oblique injury has sidelined Darnold in the Seahawks’ last two games. He suffered the injury during the final series of Seattle’s 34-17 loss at the hands of Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears at Lumen Field in Seattle in Week8, in which he also passed for 188 yardsa nd two touchdowns against an interception on 17-of-34 pass completions, while getting sacked three times for a loss of 17 yards. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Despite Darnold’s absence in the next two games, the reigning Super Bowl champions Seahawks have gone undefeated since he went down with the injury, with Drew Lock taking care of business under center . Seattle defeated the Arizona Cardinals at home in Week 9, 17-3, before handing Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders a 21-13 loss in Week 10 at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Lock has been a steady backup for Darnold, and the Seahawks may have as much confidence in him as they have in Darnold. In any case, Sunday’s showdown against the NFC West-leading 49ers is a crucial one for the Seahawks, who are second in the division standings with a 6-4 record but are still three wins behind the 9-1 San Francisco. item.title: PSG held to draw in Champions League as Barcelona see off Sabah
item.description: Ousmane Dembele put Paris Saint-Germain ahead from the spot (Anne-Christine POUJOULAT) Paris Saint-Germain lost their perfect record in the Champions League as Roma held them to a 2-2 draw on Wednesday, while Anthony Gordon got a brace in Baku as Barcelona eased to victory over Sabah. Bayern Munich slipped to a 2-1 loss at Lille, further denting their hopes of an automatic last-16 berth via a top-eight finish in the league phase. Liverpool cruised to a 3-0 win at Club Brugge thanks to an Alexander Isak brace either side of a fine Florian Wirtz strike, while Mauricio Pochettino and Manchester United were held to a frustrating 2-2 draw away to Sporting Lisbon. On a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, Donyell Malen's 17th goal in 16 matches this season denied Luis Enrique's twice defending champions as they failed to keep pace with Real Madrid, who are now the only remaining team with a 100 percent record in the competition. The Dutch forward's 78th-minute penalty ensured the sides finished level after Illia Zabarnyi's header and Ousmane Dembele's spot-kick had flipped the script for the hosts following Mario Hermoso's early opener for Roma. "It was the hardest match we have had this season and I am happy with the result," said PSG coach Luis Enrique. "I hope we don't have to play them later on over two legs." The result brought an end to a run of 12 consecutive wins for PSG, who have lost key attackers Desire Doue and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia to injury recently, but they nonetheless look highly likely to secure a top-eight finish and avoid the play-off round, unlike in their last two campaigns. - 'No excuses' - A point further back than PSG lie Barcelona after Hansi Flick's charges showed no signs of missing Lamine Yamal as they beat Sabah 4-1. With the teenage star out with an ankle knock, England winger Gordon continued his love affair with the Azerbaijani capital. He scored twice either side of half-time to put Barca firmly in control, taking his tally in the city to six after he scored four goals in his previous appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for previous club Newcastle last season. "I've been very successful here," Gordon said. "Two goals, I'm happy with that. "A good performance, all in all, very good." Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions before Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah. Bayern added a first defeat to their two wins and two draws so far in the competition as Vincent Kompany's injury-plagued side languish in 15th spot on eight points. "There are no excuses. It's simply the reality we face, and we have to stand together," Kompany said as Bayern tasted defeat for the first time this season. With men's Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane set for a stretch on the sidelines and Michael Olise also missing, centre-half Dayot Upamecano stepped into his illustrious colleagues' goalscoring boots to put Bayern ahead early on. item.title: Chargers reunite with cornerback they traded to Seahawks
item.description: Kiyoshi Mio-Imagn Images. Chargers reunite with cornerback they traded to Seahawks appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Los Angeles Chargers are bringing back rookie cornerback Avery Smith on a waiver claim, less than three months after trading him to the Seattle Seahawks . Los Angeles acquired a 2027 sixth-round pick in the August 30 deal. The Chargers now get another look at a player who stood out in their training camp. Smith first signed with Los Angeles in April after going undrafted out of Toledo. He worked at both outside cornerback and in the slot during his first stint with the Chargers . ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler shared news of the claim Wednesday on X, formerly Twitter, a day after Seattle waived Smith. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Chargers are claiming cornerback Avery Smith, per source — the same player they traded to Seattle in August. He was once a Chargers camp standout, now he’s back after Seattle waived him Tuesday.” Smith appeared in six games for the Seahawks, recording five total tackles while playing exclusively on special teams. Seattle waived him to make room on its 53-man roster for offensive tackle Chase Lundt, whom it signed off the Buffalo Bills’ practice squad. The Seahawks added Lundt while tackles Abraham Lucas and Charles Cross dealt with ankle injuries. At Toledo, Smith earned second-team All-MAC honors in each of his final two seasons. He totaled 100 tackles, 25 pass breakups, and three interceptions over that span. The Chargers still hold the sixth-round pick they received from Seattle. Smith rejoins a cornerback group that includes Donte Jackson, Tarheeb Still, and Cam Hart. His time with the Seahawks gives Los Angeles another player with regular-season special teams experience as it works out where he fits on defense. item.title: FAMU women's basketball can't shake slow start in Kennesaw State loss
item.description: A 10-point first-quarter deficit ended up being the impetus for Florida A&M women’s basketball dropping its third straight game. On Tuesday, the Rattlers (1-5) lost their third straight game, 81-67, at Kennesaw State , played at VyStar Arena. The KSU Owls built a 24-14 end-of-first-quarter lead that FAMU couldn’t come back from. The remainder of the quarters were fairly even, but FAMU needed to make a run to cut into the deficit. FAMU shot 25-for-55 (45%) from the field, 3-for-10 (30%) from three, and 14-for-17 from the free-throw line (82%). The Owls went 27-for-55 (49%) from the field, 8-for-25 from beyond the arc (32%), and an impressive 19-for-20 from the charity stripe (95%). KSU narrowly won the rebounding battle 28-27 and had 17 turnovers compared to the Rattlers ’ 20. FAMU’s Niah Rhodes led the team with 20 points and contributed two rebounds and four assists. Kamryn Grant had 17 points and seven rebounds. Persais Williams scored 14 points, nabbed three boards, and stole the ball four times. All are guards. KSU was led by guards Shania Nichols, 28 points, four rebounds, two assists, two blocks, and two steals, and Kaelyn Flowers, 17 points, seven assists, and three steals. The Rattlers are back in action following the Thanksgiving holiday. They will travel to Stetson (2-6) on Dec. 1 to play in head coach Bridgette Gordon’s hometown. Tip-off is at 7 p.m. on ESPN+ from the Insight Credit Union Arena at Edmunds Center. Gerald Thomas, III, is a multi-time national award-winning reporter for his coverage of the Florida A&M Rattlers at the Tallahassee Democrat under the USA TODAY Network. Follow his award-winning coverage on RattlerNews.com and contact him via email at GDThomas@Tallahassee.com or on the app formerly known as Twitter @3peatgee . This article originally appeared on Tallahassee Democrat: FAMU women's basketball can't shake slow start in Kennesaw State loss

item.title: Mauricio Pochettino fumes as Man United are “punished” in controversial Sporting draw
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino fumes as Man United are “punished” in controversial Sporting draw Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has hit out at the controversial referee calls that dearly cost his side in their dramatic 2-2 draw with Sporting CP. Controversy galore Pochettino’s wait for a first United win is set to continue following Wednesday’s draw with Sporting in Lisbon. The Red Devils were extremely hard done by as two major calls went their way, while goalkeeper Senne Lammens also endured a night to forget. Shortly before half-time, an Amad Diallo equaliser was ruled out by referee Szymon Marciniak owing to a foul committed by Youri Tielemans moments earlier. Marciniak permitted play to continue, but blew his whistle as Amad hit the crossbar, meaning that his finish seconds afterwards did not count. Replays plainly showed that Tielemans got the ball cleanly to set up Amad prior to pulling out of the challenge. Tielemans was also shown a yellow card for his troubles. Further controversy arose with ten minutes remaining as Suárez scored with an acrobatic finish after Lammens dropped the ball. United protested, but the goal stood for 2-2, and they subsequently had a goal of their own disallowed as the clock ticked down. It appeared that Kaique had scored an own goal, but after a VAR review, Patrick Dorgu was adjudged to have committed a foul on him, and the goal was chalked off. The decision appeared puzzling, given that Lammens had been subjected to equally minimal contact at the other end and Sporting’s goal was allowed to stand. To compound matters, Tielemans was shown a red card in the dying stages for a second bookable offence. Speaking to TNT Sports after the final whistle, Pochettino raged at the refereeing standards, while also praising the attitude of his players. Pochettino’s remarks The Argentine coach said, “Depends in which way you prefer. So proud of my players. It was a really tough game and I liked the team during the 90 minutes, the personality, the character.” “It’s difficult to find games a team were more punished in one game.” “Again, we were punished a lot in different actions that were key. I think everyone that watched the game saw all the actions. What I can say is I feel proud of the players and today we showed the way we want to play with everyone working together. I feel so proud. I told them after the game.” He added, “These type of situations, we need to double our effort. We need to concentrate more and focus more and try to recover better.” “With performances like today, that for me is the best medicine to prepare the next game.” “We need to really believe in our play, we need to believe more and more and more. We need to give the capacity and attitude to perform and improve things. But that is the way we need to show.” “In the second half we recovered a lot of balls in the opposite half, we were aggressive. That is the way we want to play. We need to go to the next game at Old Trafford and show that type o

item.title: MLB sues players union to boost lockout as deadline looms
item.description: Major League Baseball sued its players union in New York, hoping to secure protection from antitrust complaints in the wake of a lockout as a deadline looms to sign a new collective bargaining agreement (Mark Brown) Major League Baseball filed a lawsuit against the MLB Players Association on Wednesday seeking legal protection for a lockout expected to begin next week when their current collective bargaining agreement expires. The complaint filed in US District Court in New York seeks a declaration that a lockout would be legal under US antitrust law. The move would safeguard MLB if the players give up union status and try to sue MLB under antitrust law, exposing the league to potentially greater damages. MLB team owners have said they will not accept any new deal without a salary cap, a system the players union has successfully fought for decades. With a Tuesday deadline fast approaching, the lawsuit raised the stakes as both sides fought to determine how to divide billions of dollars in profits. "Today's filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season," MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin said. "We believe the union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to 'disclaim' its status as the players' bargaining representative to pursue an antitrust lawsuit as an end run around the bargaining process. "We have asked a federal court in the Southern District of New York to proactively disarm the union's nuclear option of disclaiming." MLBPA interim executive director Bruce Meyer called the lawsuit "completely frivolous" in a statement. "We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing." js/pnb

item.title: Awka City chosen for AfDB -funded Action Plan for Africa’s coordinated urban development
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu Awka, the capital city of Anambra State, has been selected for the African Development Bank, AfDB, – funded action plan for coordinated urban development in Africa. Under the programme, government would provide the policy direction, regulatory clarity, and institutional leadership, while development partners would support the mobilisation of technical expertise and catalytic resources. Also, the private sector is expected to play a decisive role in financing and delivering viable infrastructure and urban projects, traditional institutions, community leaders, professional bodies and residents will remain vital in safeguarding public ownership and ensuring that development stays centred on the people in the new city. At the launch of the plan on Wednesday in Awka, the state governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo said it is part of the strategic plan to create the envisioned Anambra mega city. Represented by his special Adviser on trade and commerce, Mr. Christian Udechukwu, the governor recalled that Awka is the only city chosen in Africa for the project, noting that it is because of the long term vision and the strategic implementation and the intentionality and purposeful focus of the administration. According to Udechukwu, it is the governor’s determination to transform Anambra State that drew the attention of the African Development Bank to the state. “The reforms they see here are of significance that it would serve to use Awka City as a model to prove the sustainability of the project and we are happy that this is happening under this administration”, he said. He said that a substantial amount of next year’s budget would be devoted to the development of the new Awka City, while other cities of Onitsha, Nnewi, and Ekwulobia would also undergo transformation, in addition to the new cities planned for the state. “When Awka 2.0 joins the planned industrial city, the proposed axis of prosperity would have been created. So Anambra is being positioned to become the economic hub of Nigeria and that is why the selection of Awka as a primary model sustainable city in Africa is important to us as a government. We should therefore not waste more time to move into the project preparatory stage”, Udechukwu said. Speaking at the launch, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Awka Capital Territory Development Authority, ACTDA, Dr Osita Onuko said the coordinated development framework is aimed at addressing the growing infrastructure and environmental challenges confronting Awka and guiding the capital city’s expansion towards a more liveable and inclusive future. The ACTDA boss said the action plan should be viewed not merely as a technical document, but as a shared commitment to building a productive, resilient and inclusive capital city for future generations He said: “This ambition aligns directly with the vision of His Excellency, Governor Chukwuma Soludo, to transform Anambra into a liveable and prosperous smart megacity b

item.title: Bayern Munich’s Vincent Kompany downplays effects of singular loss in Champions League
item.description: Photo by Getty Images | UEFA via Getty Images Bayern Munich suffered the bittersweet taste of defeat for the first time this season. Bayern carried a laundry list of injured players into the match on the road but still held the confidence to get the job done. Lille slowly gained momentum in the second half and generated quality chances that led to the two goals required to claim victory. In the postgame interview (via @iMiaSanMia ), Vincent Kompany acknowledged the sting of defeat but immediately turned the focus to the next challenge. “This Champions League campaign isn’t decided today,” said Kompany. “PSG haven’t even made it into the top eight before and have still won the Champions League twice under this new format. I’m not trying to sugar-coat things, but the Champions League won’t be decided today. Nevertheless, a defeat always hurts a bit.” Bayern currently sits in 15th place with eight points. They are currently closer to 8th-place Manchester City (10 points) than 25th-place Roma (5 points). It would be nice to avoid the extra two games associated with the playoff round but Bayern is talented enough to defeat every team on the path to the club’s seventh Champions League title. item.title: Steelers Player Makes Threatening Gesture at Drew Allar Amid Aaron Rodgers Crisis
item.description: A Pittsburgh Steelers player made a threatening gesture toward quarterback Drew Allar amid the team's ongoing crisis surrounding Aaron Rodgers. Getty Former Penn State quarterback Drew Allar was answering questions about Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday when Pittsburgh Steelers safety DeShon Elliott interrupted the scrum with a throat-slash gesture. Allar was the only Steelers player speaking to reporters while Rodgers, benched for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, aired grievances about the organization on national television. Elliott walked up a few minutes into the session, drew his hand across his throat and yelled “Drew!” as the scrum ended, according to Chris Adamski of the Tribune-Review . Then the session was over. Allar had come straight from practice. He knew Rodgers was on McAfee’s show, but said he could not speak on remarks being made in real time. As a rookie, he added, it was not his place to confirm or deny anything Rodgers said. Adamski described Allar as respectful throughout. Read More From Heavy Drew Allar NIL Deal: How Penn State QB Pay Compares to Oregon’s Dante Moore Allar Stays Out of Aaron Rodgers-Steelers Fight Rodgers, by contrast, held nothing back on The Pat McAfee Show . He told the host he learned of the benching from Pat Freiermuth , a tight end, and not from coach Mike McCarthy. The Steelers named Mason Rudolph the starter for the Week 12 game. Rodgers also said McCarthy fell asleep in meetings , including a quarterback meeting, and that the Steelers should release him if they intended to bench him without changing the offense. Asked whether he would return to Pittsburgh, Rodgers answered, “That ship has definitely sailed,” according to CBS Pittsburgh. Allar said none of that. He declined to confirm or deny a word of it, which left Rodgers’ account of McCarthy, the offense and the benching untouched. It was not the first time Rodgers had brought Allar into a headline. On Sept. 8, Rodgers told Cam Heyward’s Not Just Football podcast that a thread of racy direct messages about Allar had circulated through quarterback rooms. Allar, Rodgers said, has been in a long-term relationship , and “none of that was ever true.” Read More From Heavy Ex-Miami QB Carson Beck’s New NFL Contract Pays Less Than He Made in College Drew Allar’s Penn State Career and Future The Steelers drafted Allar with the 76th overall pick in the third round of April’s NFL draft and signed him to a four-year contract in July. A Medina, Ohio, native named Ohio’s Mr. Football in high school, he arrived at Penn State as an early enrollee in 2022. Allar backed up as a freshman, then started his final three Penn State seasons . Across 45 games, 35 of them starts, he threw for 7,402 yards and 61 touchdowns on 633 completions in 1,002 attempts, and went 26-9 as the starter. item.title: Man United turn Champions League into Sunday League to highlight glaring issue
item.description: Two errors from Senne Lammens denied Mauricio Pochettino his first win as Manchester United manager as his side slipped to a 2-2 draw with Sporting in a bizarre match in Lisbon. Those watching were treated to three penalties, a late red card and a ridiculous goal – courtesy of a divot in the pitch – as the sides played out a entertaining affair in the Portuguese capital. However, once again the focus will all be on United and their comedy of errors, as the visitors let a 2-1 lead slip late on in remarkable fashion. United have had several pantomime villains of late and it was the turn of the goalkeeper this time, with Lammens conceding a penalty and inexplicably dropping a simple catch to give the hosts an 80th-minute equaliser. A late error from Lammens cost United in Lisbon (PA Wire) Pochettino insisted that his players “are not fragile” in the build-up to the match but he was proven wrong in spectacular fashion here. A momentary lapse in concentration from Lammens near his own goal line turned out to be a foreshadowing, though United had settled well in Lisbon, with the visitors enjoying a long period of control midway into the first half. They lacked a cutting edge in their attacking but they at least looked comfortable, which is not something that has been said at all in recent matches. And yet once again it all changed in a matter of minutes. Lisandro Martinez, this time filling in at left-back, was once again the culprit, with the defender needlessly swinging a leg at Geny Catamo and inviting the winger to go down in the box. It was soft but it should not take away from the fact that it’s yet another high-profile mistake from the Argentine. The momentum of the game changed instantly, though United threatened to stop it when Lammens guessed the right way to stop Luis Suarez’s poor spot-kick. But there was still time for more of the ridiculous – as has been a theme at the club this season – and just minutes after saving a penalty, Lammens had conceded one . The goalkeeper ventured off his line but failed to win the challenge on Maxi Araujo, who left Noussair Mazraoui in no man’s land to latch onto the long ball and poke it past the helpless Belgian. This time, Suarez made no mistake. Lammens mistimed his challenge on __ to concede the penalty that led to the opening goal (Reuters) Sporting fans were clearly aware of United’s frailties and the Jose Alvalade was a cauldron of noise as the hosts looked to build on their lead, though the visitors managed to stem the tide as they grew back into the game. It was another decision that will raise questions and once again United seemed down on their luck as the two sides went in for half-time. item.title: European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment
item.description: Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory. Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA's Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid's 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation. But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next. "We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess," said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. "H owever, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle." Artist's illustration of the Hera spacecraft with its two deployable CubeSats, Juventas and Milani, in the vicinity of the Didymos binary asteroid system. Credit: ESA-Science Office Following up The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida . On Wednesday, ESA released Hera's first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos . The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as big as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across. Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there's no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren't sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth. " I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid," said Patrick Michel, Hera's principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. "In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen." Hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable. item.title: Malen penalty ends PSG’s perfect UCL run as Roma snatch 2-2 draw
item.description: Donyell Malen’s penalty gave Roma a 2-2 draw away to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday, as the injury-hit reigning champions saw their perfect record in this season’s competition come to an end. Malen stroked in from the spot in the 78th minute on a bitterly cold and wet night at the Parc des Princes, giving Roma a welcome point after their collapse from two goals up to lose 3-2 at Manchester United last time out. Roma had earlier taken the lead through Mario Hermoso, only for Illia Zabarnyi to equalise before substitute Ousmane Dembele put PSG briefly in front with a penalty of his own. The result ends PSG’s perfect record in this season’s league phase, and halts a run of 12 consecutive wins in all competitions for Luis Enrique’s team. They fall two points behind Real Madrid, who are now clear at the top of the standings as the only side still with a 100 percent record after five matches. It is only a minor setback for PSG in their quest to finish in the top eight of the 36-team table, and therefore qualify directly for the last 16 without having to go through the play-off round like in the last two campaigns. But the Parisians could have done with the boost of a victory as they come to terms with the loss of the outstanding Desire Doue, who may not play again this season after rupturing the ACL in his right knee last weekend. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, another of their outstanding attacking players, recently succumbed to the same injury, while Dembele has been struggling for fitness too and PSG’s prospects of winning a third straight Champions League title are undoubtedly diminished as a result. Dembele’s presence on the bench at kick-off meant that none of PSG’s five top scorers from last season were in their line-up here, with the others either injured or having departed in the case of Bradley Barcola and Goncalo Ramos. Meanwhile, Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini raised eyebrows by leaving Malen out of his starting XI. The Dutchman is running at an average of more than a goal a game this season and netted four against Parma last weekend. – Dembele spot-kick – However, Roma have been in prolific form in general, netting 26 goals in their last seven matches before arriving in the French capital. They went ahead inside five minutes here as Matias Soule cut the ball back from the byline and Spanish defender Hermoso was on hand to convert. Roma had blown even more promising leads already this season, though, losing 4-3 at home to Real Madrid after leading 3-1 with eight minutes left, and then going down 3-2 at Old Trafford despite being 2-0 ahead at half-time. Ukrainian defender Zabarnyi levelled just after the half-hour mark as he found space at the near post to head in Senny Mayulu’s corner. Evan Ndicka headed just off-target for Roma late in the first half and Niccolo Pisilli forced a good stop from Matvei Safonov early in the second half. item.title: UCL: Pochettino still winless as Man United draw 2-2 with Sporting
item.description: Mauricio Pochettino must wait for his first win as Manchester United coach after a wild 2-2 Champions League draw at Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday, with the hosts equalising thanks to a goalkeeping error from Senne Lammens. The Belgian stopper’s poor handling allowed Luis Suarez to complete a brace for the hosts, cancelling out United playmaker Bruno Fernandes’s double against his former side. United gave away two penalties in the first half, the second converted by Suarez, before Fernandes equalised from the spot early in the second half. Fernandes sent United ahead with a lucky bounce taking his effort over the Sporting goalkeeper, before Suarez’s acrobatic effort levelled the game. United midfielder Youri Tielemans was sent off in stoppage time for a second yellow card to end a compelling and often erratic match. A crushing 4-0 defeat by rivals Liverpool in the Premier League at the weekend, leaving United 19th, was a disastrous first game at the helm for Pochettino after replacing Michael Carrick. Pochettino brought Harry Maguire into the three-man defence as he shuffled his pack, as well as starting Joshua Zirkzee in place of the suspended Matheus Cunha. Neither side took many risks in the opening stages, with few chances of note until the game burst into life midway through the first half as United lost control. Lisandro Martinez brought down Geny Catamo in the area and Sporting were awarded a penalty. The hosts blew their chance from the spot, with Suarez’s scuffed effort easily saved by Lammens, but the Red Devils gave away another spot kick just a couple of minutes later. Goalkeeper Lammens came flying off his line and clattered Maxi Araujo, and this time Colombian striker Suarez made no mistake from the spot. – United unhappy with disallowed goals – United thought they had equalised when Amad Diallo hit the crossbar and then nodded home the rebound, but the goal was disallowed to their dismay. Youri Tielemans was ruled to have fouled Goncalo Inacio, although he seemed to win the ball, upsetting United further after Leny Yoro’s controversial red card against Liverpool on Sunday that was later rescinded. Fernandes pulled United level early in the second half from the spot after Eduardo Quaresma brought down Martinez. The former Sporting playmaker calmly stroked his penalty beyond the dive of Kaique Pereira into the bottom left corner. Fernandes said on the eve of the game he had stopped contract talks because he wanted to focus on helping United improve their form after a dire start to the season. The midfielder soon had his second goal, with the help of a bizarre bounce off a divot on the pitch. Fernandes’s low effort from distance seemed bound for Pereira’s hands, but suddenly bounced up off a patch of uneven turf and fortuitously over the goalkeeper’s head. The Portugal international bent a free-kick narrowly off target as he looked to complete his hat-trick. Lammens saved well from Sergi Altimira to protect United’s lead as Sporting ba

item.title: Dangote Refinery to list on Nigerian Exchange December 1
item.description: The Dangote Petroleum Refinery says it will begin trading on the Nigerian Exchange (NGX) Group on December 1, marking its entry into the Nigerian stock market following its initial public offering (IPO). Devakumar Edwin, vice-president of oil and gas at Dangote Group, announced the development on Wednesday, according to a Reuters report. The listing comes after the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) approved the refinery’s share allocation plan following its heavily oversubscribed IPO, which closed last month. The regulatory approval cleared the way for the company to distribute shares to investors and proceed with preparations for its stock market debut. The refinery had earlier sought to increase the size of its IPO by up to 30 per cent to approximately $2.1 billion following strong investor demand. On September 11, Aliko Dangote, president of Dangote Industries Limited (DIL), said the refinery planned to pursue a listing on a United States stock exchange after expanding its production capacity to 1.4 million barrels per day within the next two and a half years. However, on November 8, Dangote disclosed that the refinery’s IPO fell short of its target of attracting 10 million investors. Despite missing the target, Africa’s richest person said the offer attracted “millions of investors”. He described the level of participation as significant when compared with some of the largest public offerings in Africa and globally. item.title: December full moon 2026: When, where and how to see the Cold Moon
item.description: null The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, according to the Old Farmer's Almanac . December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear 30% brighter and 14% larger than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon).. According to the late, great astronomer Fred Espenak , the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026! When to see the December full moon The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker for timings specific to your location. Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects. A yellow full moon rises over Italy. (Image credit: Photo by Lorenzo Di Cola/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes. The table below details moonrise timings for a selection of cities spread across the globe for Dec. 23-24: Local moonrise timings for the December 2026 full Cold Moon City Local time New York 3:58 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 London 4:07 p.m. GMT on Dec. 24 Tokyo 4:32 p.m. JST on Dec. 24 Beijing 4:55 p.m. CST on Dec. 24 Sydney 8:36 p.m. AEDT on Dec. 24 Why it's called the Cold Moon The December full moon is often called the Cold Moon in reference to the often freezing temperatures that can descend this time of the year. It's also known as the " Long Night Moon " by the Mohican tribe of North America, because of its proximity to the winter solstice, which marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere. Old English peoples knew it as the "Moon Before Yule", according to Time and Date , while the Celts of Europe referred to it as the Oak Moon after traditions that centered around the hardy trees. The December full moon also coincides with the Hindu festival of Datta Jayanti, when followers gather to celebrate the birth of Lord Dattatreya, who embodies the Hindu holy trinity of Lord Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, according to t

item.title: Troops rescue 5 kidnapped victims, arrest 2 suspected terrorists in Kaduna
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma in furtherance of ongoing counter-terrorism operations, on Wednesday successfully rescued 5 kidnapped victims and arrested of 2 suspected terrorists in separate operations conducted in Kaduna State. Confirming the rescue operation, Captain Sinivie Tamuno, Spokesman said, “On Wednesday, 25 November 2026, troops of Sector 1 responded to distress calls following attacks by suspected terrorists on Dan Bushiya community in Chikun Local Government Area, during which some residents were abducted. “Despite encountering an ambush, troops continued their rescue efforts without sustaining any casualties. “The operation led to the rescue of a woman and her baby, who were abandoned by the fleeing terrorists following sustained pressure from the troops. “Similarly, on the same day, troops responded to another distress call following the abduction of 5 residents of Kakura village in the same Local Government Area. “The swift intervention of the troops forced the terrorists to abandon 3 of the kidnapped victims, who were subsequently rescued. “Efforts are ongoing in conjunction with other security agencies to track and eliminate the terrorists. “In a related development, on the same day, a joint patrol team conducting search and rescue operations following a kidnapped incident in Danbushiya community, found a national ID card along the terrorists’ withdraw route. “The discovery subsequently led to the arrest of the bearer identified as Mr Shauibu Musa and another suspect named Aliyu Ahmed. “The suspected terrorists are in troops custody for further investigation. The Joint Task Force Operation Fansan Yamma remains resolute in its commitment to combating terrorism and other forms of criminality, securing lives and property, and restoring lasting peace across the North West. “Members of the public are urged to continue supporting ongoing operations by providing timely and credible information on suspicious activities to the troops and other security agencies.” The post Troops rescue 5 kidnapped victims, arrest 2 suspected terrorists in Kaduna appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
item.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. He also called on countries yet to ratify the treaty, particularly African nations, to do so, pledging Nigeria’s commitment to working wi

item.title: On this day in space! Nov. 25, 1970: NASA's 'wingless' M2-F3 'lifting body' aircraft makes its 1st powered flight ahead of supersonic tests
item.description: null On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight. The M2-F3 aircraft was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft. After Air Force test pilot Bill Dana took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights. The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet. NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind. In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the M2-F2 lifting body , after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said. "When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA wrote in an overview . Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation. "A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," NASA wrote . "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft." If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the National Air and Space Museum in Washington, D.C. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

item.title: “I Don Finally Make My Mama Proud”: Asisat Oshoala Graduates With a Master’s Degree
item.description: Super Falcons striker Asisat Oshoala in her graduation gown and cap at Wembley Stadium after earning her MSc in International Sports Management. Super Falcons striker Asisat Oshoala has added a brand-new title to her name—and this time, it comes with a graduation cap and gown. The Nigerian football star graduated today, Wednesday, 25 November 2026, with a Master of Science (MSc) degree in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sport (GIS) at a ceremony held at Wembley Stadium in London. Sharing photos from the graduation on her Instagram Story, the forward kept her caption short, sweet, and full of charm: “I don finally make my mama proud.” Long before collecting European trophies and continental awards, the Ikorodu-born athlete attended Aunty Ayo International School in Lagos, where she first started playing football before pursuing the sport professionally. Now, alongside her playing career, she holds a postgraduate master’s degree in sports management—equipping herself for leadership roles off the pitch as well as on it. Asisat Oshoala holds two bouquets of flowers while celebrating her Global Institute of Sport graduation at Wembley Stadium. On the field, Oshoala remains one of Africa’s most decorated footballers. Playing primarily as a centre-forward—and occasionally out wide as a winger—the 32-year-old represents Nigeria on the international stage as a key pillar of the Super Falcons, and currently plays club football in the Saudi Women’s Premier League for Al-Hilal, following spells with Arsenal, Liverpool, Dalian Quanjian, FC Barcelona Femení, and Bay FC. Her footballing CV speaks for itself. A six-time CAF African Women’s Footballer of the Year—the first player in history to win the honour six times—Oshoala has won multiple UEFA Women’s Champions League trophies with Barcelona, claimed Liga F and Women’s Super League titles, and represented Nigeria across multiple FIFA Women’s World Cups and Olympic Games. Beyond football, she also runs the Asisat Oshoala Academy and Foundation, which empowers young girls in Nigeria through sports and education. Asisat Oshoala celebrates her Global Institute of Sport graduation at Wembley Stadium alongside her mother and loved ones. Asisat Oshoala celebrates her Master of Science degree in International Sports Management at Wembley Stadium. item.title: Google search alternative Kagi launches Gmail rival
item.description: Kagi, a small, Palo Alto, California-based software company that provides a subscription-based search engine as an alternative to Google, has launched a Gmail-like e-mail service. Dubbed Kagi Mail, it makes many of the same claims as the search engine product: privacy, personal data sovereignty, customization, and control. Additionally, Kagi is rolling out a calendar as part of the mail service. Right now, both the email and calendar interfaces are web-only, but native Android and iOS apps are planned for the fourth quarter of next year. The email interface, currently in public beta, is minimalist. It emphasizes keyboard commands, as well as a private and ad-free experience. (You can see more details in Kagi's blog post about what they mean by private.) Other feature offerings include unlimited aliases and domains, an anti-lock-in policy for user data, 50GB of storage, rule-based filtering with Sieve, an MCP server, and several optional, off-by-default AI features, like chatting with an agent to search email history, do large-scale re-labeling, or define additional filtering rules. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: APC’s Strategy Is To Ensure NDC Candidates Can’t Campaign Nationwide — Olumide Akpata
item.description: A former president of the Nigerian Bar Association, Olumide Akpata, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of plotting to frustrate candidates of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and prevent them from campaigning across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. Akpata, who is a chieftain of the NDC, spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today while reacting to the attack on members of the party by armed hoodlums in Benin City, ahead of the visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to Edo State, on Wednesday. He decried the intimidation and hostility shown by the APC against the NDC, saying that two facility owners the opposition party had paid to have their town hall meeting in Benin City refunded the payment when they received calls not to allow the event to hold there. Akpata, who contested the Edo State governorship election in 2024, also recalled how hoodlums invaded his office in the state capital and opened fire. He called on the ruling APC to allow Nigerian voters to decide whether they have done well, rather than resort to violence. While responding to a question about the rig-and-die slogan attributed to the NDC, Akpata said anybody caught rigging should face the full wrath of the law. The former NBA president said that the NDC will not back down in the face of intimidation. He also said that the opposition party would ensure that the matter is not swept under the carpet. “We are not going to sink to the despicable depths these other persons are willing to do,” he added. item.title: ‘Five bullets’ — NDC supporter recounts attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team in Delta
item.description: A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has recounted how gunmen allegedly shot him five times during an attack on the campaign team of Ovie Omo-Agege, the party’s candidate for Delta Central, in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The survivor, who sustained gunshot injuries to his chest and mouth, narrated his ordeal in a video shared on the NDC’s X page on Wednesday. The video showed him speaking from his hospital bed during a visit by Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, its vice-presidential candidate, to survivors of the attack. Recounting events leading up to the shooting, the man said he had received threats after participating in a 10,000-man march organised by the NDC in Delta State. According to him, his wife received a telephone call from individuals who threatened to shut down his business. “To be very precise, on Sunday, when we were in church, in the early hours of the day, they went and sealed the whole business premises. I could not get access to the premises; I could not offload my goods,” he recalled. “A week later, my truck that brought goods from Lagos, they seized the truck and drove it to the local government secretariat.” He said the truck was detained for more than four days, adding that no explanation had been provided for its seizure. The supporter said the attack occurred on Monday while Omo-Agege was addressing supporters at the campaign venue, when gunmen stormed the gathering and opened fire. He said one of the attackers called out his name before shooting him as he attempted to escape towards his car. “One of them started shouting, ‘That is Agba, shoot Agba, that is Agba, look at Agba going.’ Before I could say Jack, the gunshot came straight to my chest,” he said. “There is a bullet here, through the throat. There is a bullet here…five bullets on the chest and the mouth. “So, the target was just to kill me, but to God be the glory, I’m alive.” He attributed the attack to his political affiliation and support for the NDC’s presidential and vice-presidential candidates. “The whole thing is because I’m supporting NDC; I’m supporting Obi and Kwankwaso,” he said. Another survivor receiving treatment at the hospital also expressed determination to continue supporting the party despite the violence. “No matter the number of persons they shoot or attempt to kill in their time, Peter Obi will become president, Rabiu Kwankwaso will become vice-president, and Nigeria will be okay,” he said. Recall in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Nigeria Police Force spokesperson, Ani Iniedu, said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed and several others injured during the attack. Iniedu said the police would sanction any officers found to have acted improperly, unlawfully or breached professional standards during the incident. He added that an investigation was ongoing to establish the confirmed casualty figure and determine the circumstances su

item.title: Davido, Patoranking, Cubana Chief Priest to attend Odii’s Ebonyi gov’ship campaign flag-off
item.description: By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki Popular Nigerian music artists, Davido and Patoranking, as well as celebrity businessman and socialite Cubana Chief Priest, will storm, Abakaliki, Ebonyi State capital Thursday for the official flag-off of the governorship campaign of Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate, Chief Ifeanyi Chukwuma Odii. Other people expected at the event are international businessmen, politicial bigwigs and over 300 friends of Odii across Nigeria and beyond to support their own to actualize his dream of becoming the next governor come 2027. Odii who stated in a media roundtable pledged that his administration, if elected, will not abandon ongoing or uncompleted projects across the state, promising to prioritise continuity, accountability and proper execution of development projects. He said his campaign would be issue-based, reaffirmed his determination to pursue sustainable economic development. He explained that his administration would be guided by a comprehensive manifesto designed to address Ebonyi State’s present realities, past challenges and future development aspirations. According to him, the manifesto would serve as a roadmap for governance, clearly outlining the promises and programmes his administration intends to implement from the beginning of its tenure. The PDP governorship candidate maintained that governance should not be about making unrealistic political promises but about identifying existing projects, assessing their relevance and ensuring that viable investments are completed and put to productive use. “We will never abandon any project. If we must do it, we will have to do it properly,” he declared. Odii further promised to conduct a comprehensive assessment of ongoing and abandoned projects across the state to determine the resources and interventions required to complete them. He also stressed the importance of strengthening the state’s economy, noting that a stronger economic base would improve the government’s capacity to deliver infrastructure and other development commitments. On the issue of political violence, intimidation and thuggery, Odii condemned all forms of electoral violence, assuring supporters that his political ambition was driven by a genuine desire to bring about a change in governance. He expressed confidence that intimidation and other political attacks would not derail his ambition. “We mean business. We are not joking. We are fighting for a change in government. We know it, but by the grace of God, nothing can stop us,” he said. Odii, in turn, expressed his campaign’s readiness to strengthen its media engagement and public communication strategy to reach more residents across the rural and urban areas of the state. The PDP guber candidate later inaugurated his campaign council led Ambassador Nwanne Ominyi as Director General where he charged them to based their campaign on Issue-based not name calling or character assisination. item.title: 4 African countries to have produced Miss Universe winners
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African contestants have earned the Miss Universe crown six times, across four countries. South Africa leads with three wins, while Namibia, Botswana and Angola have each won once. The titleholders claimed their crowns between 1978 and 2019, giving each country a place in the pageant’s history. The latest milestone achieved by an African nation is from Miss Universe 2024 where Nigeria’s Chidimma Adetshina finished as first runner-up and was named Miss Universe Africa and Oceania. That was a notable result for Nigeria, but it did not add another country to the list of African Miss Universe winners as the overall crown went to Denmark’s Victoria Kjær Theilvig. Here are the four African countries ranked by the number of Miss Universe crowns their representatives have won. South Africa: three wins South Africa has won the title three times. Margaret Gardiner became the country’s first winner in 1978. Demi-Leigh Nel-Peters won in 2017, and Zozibini Tunzi followed in 2019. Tunzi was the third South African winner and the first Black South African woman to earn the crown. Namibia: one win Michelle McLean won Miss Universe in 1992, becoming the first and, according to the pageant’s official profile, so far the only Namibian woman to win. The win came two years after Namibia gained independence in 1990. Botswana: one win Mpule Kwelagobe won the title in 1999. She remains the only woman from Botswana to be crowned Miss Universe, according to the pageant’s official legacy page. Angola: one win Leila Lopes won Miss Universe in 2011, becoming the first Angolan titleholder. The official Miss Universe legacy page records her win and notes that she later served as national director of Miss Angola Universe. item.title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday. The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup. Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24. What the amended bill does The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile. The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.” After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release. Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims. The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight. States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them. Changes from Begich’s original version The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts. Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities.
