item.title: Gordon hits brace as Barcelona cruise to 4-1 Sabah win
item.description: Anthony Gordon struck twice as Barcelona eased to a 4-1 victory at Sabah in the Champions League to boost their chances of a top eight league phase finish. Karim Adeyemi and Gabriel Jesus also found the net for the Spanish champions as they triumphed in Azerbaijan at the Baku Olympic stadium. The Catalan giants were without teenage star Lamine Yamal for the long journey east, but found their rhythm after a slow start to claim the three points and a fourth win from five matches in the Champions League. Despite Yamal’s absence, Barca coach Hansi Flick also chose to rest Raphinha, handing Jesus a rare start up front since his summer move from Arsenal. Khayal Aliyev fired a good early chance straight at Joan Garcia as Sabah threatened in attack, against Barca’s notably fragile defence. Barca midfielder Pedri was denied at the other end before Sabah hit the crossbar, with Ivan Lepinjica’s looping effort beating Garcia but not the woodwork. Gordon broke the deadlock in the 31st minute after Sabah goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov pushed Adeyemi’s cross into his path. The England international netted four goals in his prior appearance in Baku, against Qarabag for Newcastle last season, and was Barca’s brightest player. Gordon had a second effort ruled out for offside against Jesus in the build-up, before the interval. The winger struck six minutes into the second half after Jesus’s effort was saved and the rebound came his way. It was the first of three goals in 10 minutes for the Catalan giants, with Adeyemi notching after Alejandro Balde crossed for him. Jesus bundled home Barca’s fourth of the night from almost on the goalline after Pokatilov parried Jules Kounde’s header. Barcelona had kept a clean sheet against Aston Villa in their previous European clash, after conceding in the previous 18, but were unable to add another. Joy-Lance Mickels pulled one back for Champions League debutants Sabah with a cool finish after Christian Nwachukwu pulled the ball across for him. Adeyemi crashed a shot off the bar as Barcelona threatened sporadically in the final stages without adding to their already ample tally. item.title: Meet Funmi Ojo, the University of Ibadan Graduate Who Earned a Perfect 7.0 CGPA
item.description: Doctoral scholar and University of Ibadan alumna Funmi Ojo. There are academic achievements that make you admire a person’s brilliance, and then there are stories that make you think about what determination, self-belief and a second chance can make possible. For Funmi Ojo , earning a perfect CGPA of 7.0/7.0 was about more than getting excellent grades. It was a promise she had made to herself, one shaped by an undergraduate experience in which she felt she had not quite lived up to her own academic potential. This time, she was determined to give herself nothing less than her very best. And she did. Funmi emerged as the Best Graduating Student in the Department of Pharmaceutics and Industrial Pharmacy at the University of Ibadan for the 2024/2025 academic session, completing her MSc in Drug Formulation Science with a perfect 7.0/7.0 CGPA. A Cosmetic Scientist with a B.Pharm from the same university, she is now a doctoral scholar, taking her academic journey into its next chapter. But how do you pursue a perfect score while running a growing business, building a laboratory and making room for the other parts of your life? In this interview with BellaNaija, Funmi talks about the decision to aim for a perfect CGPA from the very beginning, the study systems that helped her get there, and the lessons she learnt about time management, discipline and making the most of every mark. She also shares her thoughts on using AI as a learning tool, tackling difficult courses and knowing when to put everything else aside and focus on the goal. At what point did you realise you were chasing a record-breaking grade? Was it a goal from Day 1, or did it evolve? It was a goal from day one. About three weeks into my MSc programme, I had already decided that I wanted a perfect score. I felt I owed it to myself, particularly because I hadn’t achieved the first-class degree I wanted during my undergraduate years. It took getting to 300 level before I became more intentional about my academics, and by then, I realised I was capable of getting excellent grades. I had also seen how much strong academic results could change the trajectory of some of my colleagues, and I didn’t want to feel that I had shortchanged myself. I knew I wanted to get it right this time. Funmi Ojo, Best Graduating Student in the Department of Pharmaceutics and Industrial Pharmacy at the University of Ibadan. Interestingly, my MSc years were also when I took my business most seriously. It was growing rapidly, and I was building my own laboratory, so I had quite a lot to manage alongside my studies. During my undergraduate years, I sometimes blamed my business commitments for my academic performance, but I later realised that I had to learn how to manage my time better. I became more intentional about how I used each hour and stopped making excuses for the things I wanted to achieve. item.title: The security of US water systems is even leakier than we thought
item.description: American water systems are even less secure than we thought, according to a study of 236 technology vendors that provide gear to US drinking water, wastewater, and industrial water systems. The federal government has issued 4,014 security advisories for industrial control systems and cataloged 1,792 vulnerabilities known to have been exploited in cyberattacks. A new index, called Water Supply Chain Watch and published by exposure management firm Securin, however, found almost twice as many vulnerabilities as public records identified – including 20 exploited flaws that weren't even in the federal government's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog. The security provider compared data on water-tech vendors with records from the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), the FBI, and WaterISAC, drawing on CISA advisory data through November 20 and KEV catalog entries through November 23. It found that federal water advisories hit their highest level this year since 2020. However, the volume of security alerts isn't a reliable predictor of real-world attacks, the researchers noted. Five vendors – Rockwell Automation (58), Advantech (48), Schneider Electric (35), Siemens (26), and ABB (24) – account for 191 of the 376 water-tagged security advisories. The No. 2 firm, Advantech, accounted for the highest number of vulnerabilities rated critical, but none of the CVEs in its advisories appear in CISA's KEV catalog. Unitronics, on the other hand, accounted for only two water-tagged security advisories, but at least 75 of its controllers were compromised between November 2023 and January 2024 by attackers taking advantage of default or missing passwords. The report also highlights another disconnect between water-related CVEs and real-world cyberattacks, which don't always require attackers to exploit software bugs. The July intrusions, which security researchers suspect were the work of Iran-linked attackers , targeted more than 100 water systems , with incidents reported across at least 12 states , and involved poorly secured internet-connected controllers . According to Securin, 791 Rockwell MicroLogix 1400 controllers across multiple industries in the US were exposed to the internet as of November 17. Additionally, research by Forescout cited by the security shop found that most exposed Rockwell controllers in the US – seven in 10 – sit on mobile carrier networks, where poorly secured cellular modems can provide an entry point for attackers. A CISA advisory from July describes this technique: The authoring agencies observed Iranian-affiliated APT actors using several foreign-based IP addresses to access internet-facing PLCs manufactured by Rockwell Automation/Allen-Bradley, Schneider Electric, Siemens, and potentially other manufactured PLCs [ T0883 ]. item.description: Super Falcons forward Asisat Oshoala has added another milestone to her illustrious career after graduating with a Master of Science degree in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sports. A viral video circulating on social media showed the Nigerian football star being called up among the graduands during the institution’s graduation ceremony, drawing attention to her latest academic achievement. Super Falcons icon Asisat Oshoala has added another milestone to her career, graduating with an MSc in International Sports Management from the Global Institute of Sports. Six-time African Player of the Year, excelling on and off the pitch! pic.twitter.com/UEklwPSevX — Brila Media (@Brilamedia) November 25, 2026 Oshoala, widely regarded as one of Africa’s most successful female footballers, has enjoyed an impressive career spanning several top clubs in Europe and Asia. The six-time African Women’s Footballer of the Year has represented clubs including Arsenal, Barcelona and Bay FC, winning several domestic and continental honours. Oshoala’s graduation also adds to the growing list of Nigerian footballers combining professional football with academic pursuits. Super Eagles striker Taiwo Awoniyi is among those who have recently earned academic qualifications. The forward graduated with Merit from the Professional Footballers’ Association (PFA) Business School in September 2026, earning a Postgraduate Diploma in Global Football Sport Directorship. Awoniyi described the achievement as another proud moment away from the pitch, noting that his football career had not stopped him from pursuing education. “I have always believed that being a footballer shouldn’t stop you from being a student of the game, and education has become an important part of that journey for me,” he said. The forward had previously obtained a degree in Business Management from Buckinghamshire New University in 2022. item.title: 2027 election: Why attack NDC if Obi has no path to victory? Akpata asks
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain Olumide Akpata says the party believes its presidential candidate Peter Obi has a path to victory in 2027 and should be allowed to campaign without intimidation. Akpata spoke on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday while reacting to political violence in Edo State. On Wednesday, the Edo State Police Command confirmed that gunmen opened fire on supporters gathered along Airport Road to welcome Obi to Benin City, leaving one person injured. “Everyone is entitled to their own permutations. You know, everyone is entitled to their own back-of-the-envelope calculations regarding what the outcome will be, right? Which general goes to war without first counting the cost, as the good book says? So, for me personally, indeed, for those of us in the NDC, our permutations would seem to suggest that there is indeed a pathway,” Akpata said. Questioning the APC’s confidence ahead of the election, the former president of the Nigerian Bar Association asked why the NDC was being prevented from campaigning if it had no prospect of winning. “If you are that confident, why are your minions and why are those who are acting on your behalf making it difficult for the NDC to campaign? If you are that confident that there’s no pathway, why not leave us to what you consider to be our folly? Leave us alone. Let us continue to delude ourselves. Let us stay where we are. We are fine with that,” he said. “But why come after us? Why attack my office? Why shoot Senator Omo-Agege? If you are so confident that there’s no pathway for us, let us be.” Akpata also said the NDC received advance intelligence that armed individuals planned to infiltrate its town hall meeting. “We got intel this morning that the plan was for some individuals to infiltrate our town hall meeting and come in with attire, with our old NDC caps and T-shirts, and then cause mayhem. Come in armed and cause mayhem,” he said. He added that the warning was shared with security agencies after friends and family in Benin City also contacted him with concerns. “I got the intel. Quite a number of other persons got it. A lot of my friends and family in Benin City who had received this information called me out of concern, understandably so. So we had to escalate. We had to send the information to the police. We had to send the information to the State Security Service and all of that,” he said. According to Akpata, the planned disruption did not occur inside the town hall meeting. “At the town hall meeting, no such thing happened.” The legal practitioner alleged that the party’s office was attacked after NDC members had left, and said the attack was intended to intimidate them into abandoning the campaign. “They knew we had left the office. They were probably hoping that one of the staff there would get hit, and then we would be so scared that everybody would shrink into their own corner and be afraid to continue with this contest,” he said T

item.title: NASA Enhances Supplier Program, Announces Mentor-Protégé Agreement
item.description: NASA’s Office of Small Business Programs (OSBP) hosted a ceremonial Mentor-Protégé Agreement signing between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace on Oct. 29, 2026, at the U.S. Space and Rocket Center in Huntsville, Alabama. Pictured in the front row, from left to right, are Pauline Sevigny, president and owner, GRACE Aerospace; Christian Diamond, Mentor-Protégé Program manager, The Boeing Company; and Dwight Deneal, assistant administrator, OSBP. Pictured in the back row, from left to right, are Danielle Barnes, small business specialist, OSBP; Grant Crawford, Logan Ojermark, Nikki Howard, and Sabrina Pearson, contracting officers, NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) stages team; Christen Edwards, lead, SLS stages team; Bradley Niese, NASA’s senior procurement executive, deputy chief acquisition officer, and assistant administrator, Office of Procurement; Chris Hall, program manager, OSBP; and Kristina Parmenter, procurement officer, NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center. Credit: Justin Fields, Light Rain Studio How NASA works with small businesses is evolving, and as a result, the agency is strengthening the domestic aerospace industrial base to support future exploration missions through its recently renamed Small Business Supplier Development Program. As part of the program, NASA announced its latest Mentor-Protégé Agreement, this one signed between The Boeing Company and GRACE Aerospace. NASA is streamlining the application process for the Small Business Supplier Development Program, as well as reducing administrative requirements, accelerating review and approval timelines, and enhancing incentives for prime contractor participation. These improvements are aimed at making supplier development more accessible, efficient, and closely aligned with NASA’s mission needs. “We have intentionally redesigned the program as a mission-focused tool for strengthening industrial base readiness and mission success,” said Dwight Deneal, assistant administrator, Office of Small Business Programs, NASA Headquarters in Washington. “By simplifying participation and focusing developmental assistance on the capabilities NASA needs most, we are helping build a stronger, more resilient supplier base that can support the agency’s highest-priority missions.” Under the new Mentor-Protégé Agreement, Boeing will provide structured assistance to help GRACE expand its capabilities as a supplier of mission-critical aerospace hardware. Boeing will fund the agreement, valued at nearly $500,000. “Boeing is proud to continue its longstanding relationship with NASA in support of its mission and the opportunities this agreement creates for Boeing, GRACE, and the broader aerospace industrial base,” said Christian Diamond, Mentor-Protégé Program manager and small business liaison officer for Boeing. “Through this partnership, Boeing looks forward to sharing our expertise to support the continued growth and long-term success of a small business while strengthening our supplier base.”

item.title: Nigeria needs experienced, courageous leaders to tackle challenges, Amaechi hails Atiku at 80
item.description: Former Minister of Transportation, Rotimi Amaechi, has congratulated former Vice President Atiku Abubakar on his 80th birthday, saying Nigeria needs leaders with the experience, courage and capacity to address its economic and security challenges. Amaechi, in a birthday message issued on Wednesday, described Atiku as a distinguished statesman, entrepreneur, philanthropist and patriot whose contributions to Nigeria’s political, economic and social development remained significant. Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), turned 80 on Wednesday. Amaechi, a former governor of Rivers State, recalled Atiku’s tenure as Vice President between 1999 and 2007, noting his role in consolidating the Fourth Republic and driving economic reforms. He also highlighted Atiku’s leadership of the National Council on Privatisation, saying his contributions reflected his belief in private-sector development and an enabling business environment. The former minister also commended Atiku’s entrepreneurial investments in agriculture, logistics and real estate, as well as his establishment of the American University of Nigeria, Yola. He said the university reflected Atiku’s commitment to education and human capital development. Amaechi further acknowledged Atiku’s philanthropic activities, particularly his support for educational opportunities for disadvantaged Nigerians and young people affected by the Chibok tragedy. Looking ahead to the 2027 general election, Amaechi said Nigeria required leadership capable of restoring economic confidence, strengthening national security, improving education and healthcare, and ensuring reliable electricity supply. He also backed Atiku’s proposed reintroduction of petroleum production subsidy, arguing that the policy could reduce transportation costs and ease the burden of rising prices on households. According to Amaechi, Nigeria needs a people-centred development agenda that prioritises entrepreneurship, technological innovation, human capital development and private-sector-led growth. He expressed confidence in Atiku’s ambition to contest the 2027 presidential election, saying the country needed leaders who understood its challenges and were prepared to take difficult decisions. Amaechi also called for a Nigeria where young people could find opportunities at home, farmers could prosper, businesses could grow and citizens could access quality education regardless of their backgrounds. He wished Atiku good health, wisdom and strength, while commending his contributions to public service, education, philanthropy and the country’s democratic development. “At 80, your journey is not merely a story of past accomplishments but a reminder that experience must be deployed in the service of the future,” Amaechi said. The post Nigeria needs experienced, courageous leaders to tackle challenges, Amaechi hails Atiku at 80 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Seabird ‘spies’ could help spot ships that aren’t broadcasting their location
item.description: A northern gannet ( Morus bassanus ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail Steve Votier Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track. Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage. In fact, recent research suggests that three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels don’t use the technology, says Jonathan Rutter at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU). Advertisement Read more Most large fishing boats go untracked as ‘dark vessels’ Rutter says that being caught as bycatch in fishing is one of the greatest risks to seabird populations, but if fishing vessels are only tracked “with conventional methods, such footprints of risk may be strikingly incomplete”. The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( Morus bassanus ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast. Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( Puffinus mauretanicus ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. But given the high vessel density where they were – off the Catalan coast – the researchers estimated that up to 20 per cent of the vessels detected by the four birds weren’t broadcasting their identity. Tammy Davies at BirdLife International – a global partnership of non-governmental organisations – who wasn’t involved in the study, says the research could “give us a more complete picture of the risks seabirds face at sea” and “ultimately, this could contribute to better assessments of bycatch risk and help identify fisheries and areas where conservation measures are most needed”. Peter Ejbye-Ernst at the Netherlands Institute for the Study of Crime and Law Enforcement (NSCR), describes the study as “fascinating” from a green criminology point of view, too. A tagged northern gannet coming in to land in Wales Steve Votier “What this study is somewhat proposing is that we can also look outside of humans for witnesses too,” he says, which overcomes a key barrier in observing crime at sea. item.title: SpaceX Starship debris becomes art in Ashley Zelinskie's 'The Weight of Space' (video, photos)
item.description: null When a SpaceX Starship broke apart over Turks and Caicos in Jan. 2025, pieces of its heat shield washed ashore. Some of that material now hangs on a gallery wall in New York City, embedded in artist Ashley Zelinskie's print of the very explosion it survived. Look closely at the print and you can see little flakes on the surface. Some of Zelinskie's friends vacationing on the islands had come across pieces of heat-shield tile. "I think you might want these," Zelinskie recalled one friend telling her. She did. The Brooklyn-based artist ground the fragments into dust and worked them into the print. Ashley Zelinskie incorporated dust from recovered SpaceX Starship heat-shield tiles into this print of the vehicle breaking apart over Turks and Caicos. (Image credit: Ashley Zelinskie) The Starship print is part of "Ejecta," which captures rocket plumes and explosions on paper. It's one of four series in Zelinskie's solo exhibition, "The Weight of Space," which opened Nov. 20 at Heft Gallery in Manhattan. Her marble sculptures in "Monuments" depict the Hubble Space Telescope, retired NASA astronaut Mike Massimino's spaceflight gear and more. Five "Launch Sequence" sculptures follow a rocket through liftoff, and the interactive "Crowded Sky" lets visitors track what's currently orbiting overhead in real time. Zelinskie gave Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik and me a tour before the gallery doors opened. Massimino joined her that evening to celebrate the exhibition and their collaboration on "Monuments." You can watch the tour in the video above. Monuments Massimino turned up in our first look at Zelinskie's work, too. In 2022, I photographed the two of them beside her "Exploration JWST" sculpture at "Unfolding the Universe: First Light," an exhibit inspired by the James Webb Space Telescope's first images. Four years later, Massimino stood in a New York gallery looking at another Zelinskie sculpture. "That's my arm there," he told Malik. Artist Ashley Zelinskie and Space.com Editor-in-Chief Tariq Malik discuss the sculpture between them, which depicts astronaut Mike Massimino’s bare hand gripping a replica of the handrail he pulled off the Hubble Space Telescope in 2009. (Image credit: Future/Steve Spaleta) In that hand is a piece of hardware Malik remembers watching Massimino wrestle with in real time. During NASA's final Hubble servicing mission in 2009, a stripped bolt left a handrail blocking access to the telescope's Space Telescope Imaging Spectrograph (STIS). Mission Control instructed Massimino to forcibly remove the handrail so he and fellow spacewalker Michael Good could get on with the repair. Massimino told Malik that pulling the handrail off Hubble brought back a childhood memory of his father and his Uncle Frank driving a long screwdriver through a stuck oil filter. "Then my uncle Frank pulled to get more leverage, and that's what was going through my mind when I pulled off that handrail," Massimino said. He remembered looking down

item.title: Green light for Starmind: SpaceX gets approval to deploy 1 million AI satellites
item.description: null Earth orbit could get a lot more crowded in the coming years. The U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) just granted SpaceX approval to deploy one million of its Starmind AI data-center satellites in orbit. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America's leadership and growth," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said today (Nov. 25) in a statement announcing the approval. AI has become central to SpaceX's business plans and identity over the past year or so. For example, the company has said that it's eyeing a "total addressable market" of $28.5 trillion over the long haul — and nearly $23 trillion of that is in "enterprise AI applications." Starmind is key to those lofty ambitions. SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk believes that the future of AI compute is in space, where energy (from the sun ) is unlimited and there are no land-owning neighbors to lodge NIMBY complaints. SpaceX aims to launch the first of its Starmind satellites in the third quarter of 2027. The spacecraft will fly on the company's fully reusable Starship megarocket, which has deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink satellites on its most recent two test flights . Those 52 spacecraft are the vanguard of another enormous constellation: Musk has said that the next-gen Starlink network will eventually consists of about 100,000 satellites . The planned numbers for Starlink and Starmind are truly mind-boggling. To put them into perspective: Since the dawn of the space age in 1957, humanity has launched a total of just 28,000 satellites, give or take a few hundred. And the biggest constellation ever operated to date, the current iteration of Starlink, consists of about 11,000 spacecraft. These coming buildouts will require an enormous number of launches. Starship can carry a maximum of 60 V3 Starlink satellites per launch, for instance, so it will take about 1,700 liftoffs just to assemble that network (and more to maintain it, as the operational life of each satellite is expected to be about five years). Putting so many satellites into orbit also raises the risks of collisions. SpaceX has proven to be extremely proficient in this regard with its current Starlink satellites, which can detect and avoid potential collisions autonomously. But more evasive maneuvers will be required as space gets more and more crowded. SpaceX isn't the only company that aims to operate data centers in space; Cowboy Space , Starcloud, Blue Origin and Google, among other companies, have voiced similar ambitions. Starcloud and Google , in fact, have already launched AI pathfinder satellites. "Compute campuses or data centers are essential to sustaining America's leadership in SI," Carr said in the same statement. ("SI" stands for super intelligence, the Trump administration's preferred term for AI.) item.title: Saraki cautions Kwara Gov over treatment of traditional rulers
item.description: Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has urged Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq to respect traditional rulers and allow them receive political leaders across party lines. Saraki made the call following allegations that the governor had summoned some traditional rulers to Ilorin and threatened to suspend those who received leaders of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during courtesy visits to their palaces. In a statement personally signed by him, Saraki said the alleged actions followed his stakeholder engagements in Kwara North Senatorial District, which began last week. He explained that visits to traditional rulers were part of established customs and protocols, adding that the royal fathers should be allowed to receive political leaders regardless of their party affiliations. Saraki said traditional rulers were fathers of all and should not be subjected to pressure over their interactions with politicians. He also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to caution Abdulrazaq, saying political differences should not prevent opposition parties from engaging communities and traditional institutions. The former Senate President recalled that during the 16 years the PDP governed Kwara State, traditional rulers were not prevented from receiving opposition leaders. He said democracy required tolerance of opposing views and urged the governor to respect the state’s traditional institutions. Saraki, however, insisted that the alleged actions would not discourage the PDP from continuing its engagements across the state. He said the party would sustain its outreach to communities in the three senatorial districts, adding that the response to its engagements had been encouraging. Saraki Accuses Kwara Governor of Intimidating Traditional Rulers Former Senate President, Dr Abubakar Bukola Saraki, has cautioned Kwara State Governor Abdulrahman Abdulrazaq against allegedly threatening and intimidating traditional rulers over their reception of leaders of the opposition Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during campaign visits. Saraki also urged the leadership of the All Progressives Congress (APC) to call the governor to order, saying his alleged conduct was inconsistent with the democratic principles of the party. In a statement personally signed by him, Saraki alleged that since he began stakeholder engagements in Kwara North Senatorial District last week, Abdulrazaq had been summoning traditional rulers to Ilorin or threatening to suspend those who received his delegation on courtesy visits to their palaces. item.title: Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028 Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets. The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF. With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement. Exchanges only with partners that qualify Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security. Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange. The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year. The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said. Down from 74 partners The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027. Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028. That U.S. timeline is already shaping policy elsewhere. South Korea pushed its 22% crypto tax back to 2029 partly because it will not receive American crypto trading data

item.description: Some customers have raised concerns about Backblaze's privacy policy taking effect next month, which says the backup and cloud storage company may sell certain personal information to advertisers. Backblaze’s current privacy policy says that in addition to the personal information that users may provide, such as their email address when creating an account, it may also “automatically” collect information, such as “your software, the operating system you use when accessing our service, your Internet Protocol address, and the date and time of each request you make to Backblaze.” The current policy adds: “Under no circumstances do we rent, trade, or share your address or e-mail address with any other company for their marketing purposes without your consent.” It also makes no mention of advertisers. item.title: The FCC has authorized SpaceX to deploy 1 million satellites
item.description: In an extraordinary decision, the Federal Communications Commission on Wednesday granted SpaceX conditional authorization to deploy a constellation of up to 1 million Starmind satellites designed to serve as orbital data centers. If fully deployed, this constellation would increase the number of satellites in orbit by roughly 50-fold. "The United States is moving decisively to ensure that this breakthrough technology creates opportunity, drives investment, and delivers lasting benefits for the American people," FCC Chairman Brendan Carr said in a statement on Wednesday. "This action opens a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to power America’s leadership and growth." Read full article Comments

item.title: Senate Appropriations Committee session turns violent as aide, security operatives clash
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — A legislative aide to Senator Allwell Onyesoh (Rivers East) was allegedly assaulted by security operatives attached to the Senate Committee on Appropriations, chaired by Senator Olamilekan Adeola (APC, Ogun West), during a confrontation at the National Assembly complex, Abuja. The aide, Barrister Kingsley Wali, reportedly sustained head injuries during the incident and was rushed to the National Assembly Clinic for medical attention. Wali alleged that he and another aide to Senator Onyesoh, identified as Dr Kingsley, were attacked by security personnel after accompanying their principal to an Appropriations Committee meeting. Recounting the incident, Wali said the confrontation occurred after Senator Onyesoh had entered the committee room and he attempted to follow him. He said security personnel at the entrance were trying to close the door and stopped him from entering. According to him, when the operatives attempted to push his colleague away, he explained that their principal had already entered the room and that they were not attempting to force their way inside. He alleged that the situation escalated when the security personnel grabbed Dr Kingsley by the neck and began assaulting him. “I kept telling them to leave him alone because he is our senator’s personal assistant and my colleague. I even held one of the security personnel’s hands and pleaded with him to stop beating him,” Wali said. He further alleged that the operatives turned on him because he intervened on behalf of his colleague. Wali claimed that one of the security personnel grabbed him and pushed him down a staircase, while three others allegedly cornered him and repeatedly hit his head with the butt of a gun. He said the assault continued until he slumped, after which the operatives left him. According to him, Dr Kingsley subsequently took photographs of his condition and sent them to Senator Onyesoh through WhatsApp while the senator was attending the committee meeting. Wali said the senator came out after receiving the photographs and found him lying in a pool of blood. He added that the senator subsequently took him into the committee room, where members expressed shock at his condition and directed that he be taken to the hospital for treatment. Speaking about his condition, Wali said he was still weak following the alleged assault and the fall. “I’m weak. I’m completely weak because they pushed me down and I slumped. But God will take care of everything. I thank God for everything,” he said. However, Senator Adeola’s Special Adviser on Media, Kayode Odunaro, offered a different account of the incident. In a statement titled, “Security Breach at Senate Committee on Appropriations Room,” Odunaro said the confrontation followed a misunderstanding between aides of some senators attempting to gain access to a committee room during a closed-door session and security personnel stationed at the entrance. item.title: Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses. The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month. In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29. Bithumb breach ran for 15 days Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there. That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks. Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected. Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers. It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken. For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets. Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. It said it has found no sign that its exchange service systems or customer database were directly breached, and that it has stepped up real-time monitoring of unusual trades and withdrawals. Bithumb promises compensation The exchange said it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. It has also set up a dedicated support desk for victims that covers financial and legal counseling as well as compensation reviews. “We will

item.title: Nigerian woman found dead in Canada days after returning from work
item.description: A 26 year old Nigerian woman, Ayotomiwa Chelsea Omotosho, has been found dead in Canada, days after returning home from work, leaving her family and members of the Nigerian community seeking answers about the circumstances surrounding her death. Chelsea, a graduate of Humber College, was reportedly found lifeless on Thursday, November 19, 2026, after returning from work the previous day. According to a fundraising appeal launched by friends and members of the Nigerian community in Canada, the cause of her death remains unknown. “On Wednesday, November 18, 2026, Chelsea returned home from work, just as she had on countless other days. Tragically, on Thursday, November 19, she was found lifeless. At this time, the cause of her death remains unknown,” the appeal stated. Chelsea moved from Nigeria to Canada in May 2024 to study Media Management at Humber College. She graduated in November 2025 and later secured employment in the healthcare sector at The Residence on Yonge. She was also an active member of the MOLC Choir, where she became known within the Nigerian community in Canada. Friends described her as a warm and dedicated young woman, saying her sudden death had left those who knew her devastated. The youngest of four children, Chelsea is survived by her parents and siblings in Nigeria, who are now mourning her loss from thousands of kilometres away. Her family, alongside members of the Nigerian community in Canada, is making arrangements for a memorial service and burial in the country. The fundraising appeal said her loved ones were still seeking answers about what led to her death as they prepare to lay her to rest. The post Nigerian woman found dead in Canada days after returning from work appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Huawei and crew tout homegrown EDA tools to overcome China’s fab deficit
item.description: Chinese telecom and IT giant Huawei boasted about its advancements in domestic electronic design automation (EDA) software this week, which it needs to accelerate the adoption of homegrown chip manufacturing. EDA is an umbrella term for software, hardware, and services essential to the planning, design, and production of modern chips. Today, Cadence Design Systems, Synopsys, and Siemens dominate the industry, but US export controls have restricted Huawei and other blacklisted Chinese businesses' access to their tools. The US blacklisted Huawei back in 2019 over concerns the telecommunications equipment giant could be forced to inject backdoors into its gear. Unable to access top EDA tools, Huawei’s chip division, HiSilicon, was forced to develop its own with the help of Phlexing Technology. This week, Phlexing chairman Qing He detailed the company’s efforts to bring new EDA tools to support Huawei’s so-called Tau Scaling Law design philosophy. “Tau EDA is the domestic EDA tool chain for Tau chips. It comes from a long, close partnership with Huawei,” he said. We discussed the tech earlier this year, but in a nutshell, it involves using advanced packaging, specifically 3D hybrid bonding, to achieve higher transistor density for a given area. The TSMC of China, Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corporation (SMIC), is still years behind Taiwan, South Korea, and the US on process technology. It currently has the ability to mass-produce chips on the equivalent of a 7 nm process. For comparison, TSMC began producing 5 nm-class products in 2020 and commenced mass production of 2 nm-class chips in late 2025. So, Huawei aims to use 3D packaging to close the gap, but for this to happen, it first needs tools capable of designing such chips, and that’s just what Phlexing claims to have done with its GloryBolt and GloryEX platforms. “Traditional EDA has long handled only single processes. Tau EDA needs to integrate and decompose multiple processes,” He said. “Coupling multi-scale, multi-structure, and multi-physics issues called for new analysis tools.” This, He says, culminated in the co-development of a process design kit (PDK) with Huawei beginning in 2024. These technologies have now gone live. The development comes as Huawei looks to bring larger, more capable processors to market. We previously discussed the company’s latest developments around AI accelerators, near packaged optics, networking, and rack systems. Many of these advancements will depend on multi-die chip packages, enabled by EDA tools, like those built by Phlexing. ®

item.title: The Fairphone 6 Plus is modular, repairable, and $100 off right now
item.description: The Fairphone 6 Plus comes with 12 replaceable parts. | Photo: Dominic Preston / The Verge Unlike most smartphones, the Fairphone 6 Plus is designed for home repair, with easily replaceable parts that could help extend its lifespan well into the future. That makes its midrange price point easier to justify, especially now that it’s dropped to a new low of $552.49 (about $98 off) at Amazon as part of the retailer’s ongoing Black Friday sale. Fairphone 6 Plus Where to Buy: $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (black) $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (green) $649.99 $552.49 at Amazon (blue) The 6.3-inch Fairphone 6 Plus features 12 user-replaceable parts, including the battery, screen, USB-C port, and cameras, all of which you can swap out with the included screwdriver. Replacement parts are relatively affordable, too; a new battery costs $39.99, which helps offset its middling battery life and lack of wireless charging. It also comes with a five-year warranty and up to six Android OS upgrades, making it a good option if you want a phone you can keep using for years. Although repairability is its marquee feature, the 6 Plus is also a solid midrange Android device. Fairphone prioritizes ethically sourced materials , making it a strong choice for environmentally conscious buyers who don’t want to sacrifice performance. Its Snapdragon 7s Gen 4 processor handles everyday tasks well, and its cameras take decent photos, though they’re not quite on par with those of pricier phones. What’s more, it offers a clean, bloatware-free Android experience and modular back panels, which you can swap for optional accessories like a card holder or crossbody strap. Our own Allison Johnson particularly liked the phone’s dedicated switch for turning on customizable focus modes called Moments, which can simplify your homescreen and limit access to distracting apps — something we could all use a little less of. Read our full Fairphone 6 Plus review .

item.title: AI’s stunning progress in maths shows how little we understand it
item.description: MARK SYKES/SPL/Alamy There is a story, possibly apocryphal, that when the mathematician G. H. Hardy was about to undertake a dangerous sea voyage, he sent a postcard to a colleague declaring “I have solved the Riemann hypothesis”. Hardy, a staunch atheist, joked that this would prevent his ship from sinking, as God would never let him claim the credit for such a major result without revealing the details of his proof. Hardy would probably be both astonished and aghast that we now have what seems to be a proof of the Riemann hypothesis , a problem that has vexed mathematicians since the 19th century, but that no one yet understands it. The consensus among mathematicians is that the proof, produced with the aid of AI, will hold, but that it will take much more work to make it comprehensible to humans. However you feel about AI, this is a watershed moment, and one that demonstrates just how little we still understand about the capabilities of the technology. As recently as last month, leading mathematician Terence Tao speculated that AI would eventually solve the Riemann hypothesis, but that it may not happen before 2050. Now, some mathematicians are considering whether their hardest and most infamous remaining problems could be settled within months. In a year that has left mathematicians reeling, this may be the knock-out blow. Advertisement This is a watershed moment, and it shows just how little we understand about AI’s abilities For non-mathematicians, the fall of the Riemann hypothesis is harder to interpret. In the past year, AI has seen incredible advances in both maths and coding, but it is perhaps no coincidence that in these arenas, with nothing more than computer code, answers can swiftly be checked and iterated upon, allowing for rapid improvement. When it comes to other human endeavours though, from art to zoology, such verification is far harder, involving either the messy physical world, or unknowable human taste – or both. Whether this verification gap can be closed may become the biggest question of our age. Answers on a postcard, please. What is the Riemann hypothesis and why is its solution so monumental? It has been called the hardest problem in mathematics, and now through a combination of human ingenuity and relentlessness, and the computational power of AI, the Riemann hypothesis may have finally been solved

item.title: Our verdict on Dark Eden by Chris Beckett: ‘Holy cow. Chapter 44!’
item.description: The New Scientist Book Club read Chris Beckett’s Dark Eden in November Since starting the New Scientist Book Club in May 2023, I have aimed to vary our books as much as possible, moving between science fiction and popular science, older classics and the hottest new titles. Occasionally, though, I’m afraid I let the power go to my head and just choose one of my own personal favourites. That’s what I did in November, with Chris Beckett’s novel Dark Eden , a book I’ve loved ever since it won the Arthur C. Clarke award in 2013. Set on the planet Eden, a sunless world that drifts alone far outside the Milky Way, this follows the descendants of two astronauts who were marooned there over a century earlier. Now numbering 532 people, they tell each other stories of the world their ancestors came from, and struggle to survive on this dark, cold planet as they await the return of “one of those sky-boats with lights on them”. I think it is all wildly imaginative and original and exciting. So it was with some trepidation that I awaited the verdict of my fellow book club members on our Discord channel. I really wanted everyone else to love it, too! Free newsletter Sign up to Book Club Sign up to newsletter It started well. “I managed not to stay up all night reading, but the temptation was definitely there – I am hooked,” wrote Dee55. Les was similarly gripped. “Started it? I’ve only gone and finished it, haven’t I? It really got me in, and I found it a fascinating exploration of social anthropology and linguistics in a very small, isolated population. And the world-building was fascinating, too – very different flora and fauna.” Advertisement Several other members also cited the strength of the world-building in Dark Eden . I also love the lanternflowers and woollybucks of this planet, and was fascinated to learn, in an essay Chris wrote for book club members, that, when creating a world for a story, he doesn’t “usually seek to make the whole thing scientifically accurate, but I try to make it hang together in a way that feels coherent”. I think he definitely succeeds in that here. In Dark Eden, I imagined how life might exist on a sunless planet Dark Eden, the November read for the New Scientist Book Club, takes place on a rogue planet outside the Milky Way. Award-winning author Chris Beckett explains how he thought through the science behind this night world There were some excellent debates about the language these people have developed – they double up on words for emphasis, for example (“big big”; “cold cold”), use bastardised forms of our words (“Landing Veekle”; “leckytrickity”), and talk about Starry Swirl – the Milky Way they can see in their skies, a wonderfully evocative image. “I think Beckett has done something really clever here. He’s created a language that feels familiar enough to read naturally, but is sufficiently different to remind us that this is an entirely separate culture that has evolved in isolation,” wrote Maria. “I enjoyed some of

item.title: Is The Time Traveler’s Wife the perfect audiobook to experience on shuffle?
item.description: Josie Ford Feedback is our weekly column of bizarre stories, implausible advertising claims, confusing instructions and more Reader Jenny Ozanne writes to tell us of a horrific incident that befell her partner. He had bought Audrey Niffenegger’s novel The Time Traveler’s Wife as a CD audiobook, to listen to on long car journeys. “After a while, he complained that the plot was completely impossible to follow,” writes Jenny. “It was only when I checked his player that I realized he had accidentally set the CD to ‘shuffle’. “ Advertisement Jenny raises two points, which Feedback heartily endorses: “I’m still not sure what’s more impressive: the story’s ability to survive total chronological chaos, or the fact that he listened to three random chapters before suspecting anything was wrong.” Feedback would suggest that The Time Traveler’s Wife might be the ideal novel to experience on shuffle, since the narrative is heavily non-linear. The main character hops uncontrollably back and forth through history. This led us to wonder: would any similarly chrono-displaced stories survive the experience of being played on shuffle, or even be improved by it? We wondered, for instance, about David Mitchell’s Cloud Atlas . This has six stories set in different periods, including a future in which human clones are used as cheap labour, and a more distant future in which everything has gone a bit Mad Max . The stories are linked by characters in later timelines reading about the earlier ones, and by subtle coincidences. What would it be like on shuffle? However, after careful reflection, we realised there is only one correct answer to this, and that is Shane Carruth’s 2004 film Primer , which tells the story of two tech bros who invent a time machine in their garage. At first, they use it to go back in time and make money on the stock exchange, only to become caught up in an escalating web of betrayal and deception as they endlessly rewrite their lives. Primer is so overcomplicated, so mind-wreckingly confusing, that some poor soul once went so far as to draw a diagram trying to convey its timeline. Posted on Reddit by u/Clawz114, the diagram looks like a cross between a metro map and a flowchart of the inner workings of a chemical factory. It is therefore possible that playing the scenes in random order might actually cause the film to make more sense. The scent of success It’s that time of year when many of us are thinking, “Oh blimey, I need to buy everyone presents” and then having a meltdown when we can’t think of anything. The last refuge of the true gift scoundrel is, of course, the scented candle. This item might as well come with a note saying, “Sorry, I couldn’t think of anything”. Readers looking to step up their scented candle game may wish to investigate JD + Kate Industries , which is run by a pair of humour writers with a sideline in themed scented candles. item.title: ‘Blade Runner 2099’ cast praise the incredible set designs that brought the sci-fi universe to life: ‘it was all so well-realized’ (interview)
item.description: null Prime Video’s " Blade Runner 2099 " has arrived with an 8-episode limited series revealing what the "Blade Runner" world looks like 50 years after the events of director Denis Villeneuve’s "Blade Runner 2049." The most obvious change in this depressing dystopia is that replicants are running the LA show after some unmentionable ecological disaster and humans are now the ones relegated to underclass citizens. Starring Michelle Yeoh as a replicant cop named Olwen whose life clock is running out and Hunter Schafer as Cora, a desperate human posing as a replicant blade runner, "Blade Runner 2099" unties these two in a mystery revolving around a rogue blade runner and a deadly secret that might cause their city to implode. We connected with three of the sci-fi show’s main co-stars, Matthew Needham ("House of the Dragon"), Lewis Gribben ("T2 Trainspotting") and Dimitri Abold ("Love Addicts") to hear more about working with creator/showrunner Silka Louisa, and immersing themselves in " Blade Runner 2099's " vivid futuristic worldbuilding. "For me it's a lot simpler than egos because he's such a goal-oriented person and all of his stuff has such a police procedural quality to it," Needham tells SPACE regarding his role as Yahya, an emotionless replicant who despises all humans. "It was really fun to just follow what Silka [Louisa] did. She wrote this great, really exciting mystery thriller, and I just got to play in that.” Matthew Needham and Hunter Schafer star in "Blade Runner 2099" (Image credit: Amazon Prime Video) Scottish actor Gribben portrays Cora's ailing younger brother Elias, who has compromised mobility and a rocky relationship with his overprotective sister. "I've played a few characters that were fairly vulnerable or insular," he notes. "Then seeing the journey of this character grow in strength and confidence and feel like becoming his own man was so compelling to me. It’s almost a relationship that falls apart between brother and sister, and that's fascinating to me because that’s such a cool dynamic you don’t always really see in television shows. That was quite interesting and made me want to try and be in it." (Image credit: Amazon Prime Video) As Bebeto, a doctor, veteran of the replicants vs. humans war, and a black-market dealer helping his species procure IDs and passports off-world, Abold enjoyed exploring the many facets of his character. "Much like Matthew and Lewis, for me it was the journey that Bebeto goes on," Abold adds. "Starting out as someone who’s so hopeful and has to try and scrape up the last dregs of hope as things start falling apart. Being subject to circumstances like that inherently make for an interesting story arc and story in general. Throwing myself into that, especially after how well Silka crafted the story and script, was something I was totally ready for." item.title: NASA Eyes Crop Candidates for Future Menus
item.description: As NASA prepares for future missions to the Moon and Mars, researchers are studying crops that could provide astronauts with fresh food, nutrition, and variety far from Earth. Such crop variety can help with menus in deep space, something top of mind this week as the nation celebrates Thanksgiving. Strawberries grown in the Space Life Sciences Lab’s controlled environment chamber. Cucumbers are grown in a controlled environment chamber at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. Lemon basil is growing in chambers on the International Space Station. NASA Recent testing points to strawberries, cucumbers, and lemon basil as potential options for future explorers. Space crops can absorb carbon dioxide, produce oxygen, and recycle water. These capabilities will become increasingly important as crewed missions extend farther from our home planet. While space crop research advances on Earth, capabilities are also expanding in space. A new investigation from NASA’s Biological and Physical Sciences Division is set to launch to the International Space Station, where the first-of-its-kind prototype growth chamber will provide critical insights for developing crop production systems that could grow crops like these for future Moon Base habitats and Mars missions. Sweet space strawberries Strawberries are among the few sweet fruits under consideration for spaceflight and are nutritious, aromatic, and self-pollinating. Researchers at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida are growing strawberries in flight-like growth chambers to evaluate the potential space crop, and NASA partners at The Australian Research Council Centre for Excellence in Plants for Space also are helping expand knowledge of space strawberries. Researchers at NASA Kennedy, the University of Melbourne, and the University of Western Australia recently tested a wild strawberry against NASA’s leading strawberry candidate, ‘Delizz,’ to see which thrived better under simulated space conditions. Delizz and the wild strawberry produced very different fruits, according to a study published in September in the journal Life Sciences in Space Research. Delizz grew large, red fruit, while the wild strawberry produced small, yellow fruit due to a recessive genetic mutation. But looks are not everything. When grown from a seed, the wild strawberry produced twice as many buds, flowers, and fruit as Delizz. Ultimately, however, NASA’s pick kept its top spot, as the wild strawberry grew too many runners that would take up valuable room aboard a spacecraft. Cucumbers show promise Many crops have been grown in space, but none so far have come from the gourd family. Cucumbers could be the first. Before crops like cucumbers can be grown and eaten in space, they must undergo extensive testing. NASA-funded researchers recently evaluated cucumbers for their growth, yield, and nutrition under spaceflight conditions. The researchers found that while the plants showed some signs of enlarged leaves, they produced a stead

item.title: DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine DOJ Targets 800 Defendants in Largest-Ever Scam Crackdown, Including Crypto Fraud The U.S. Justice Department said Tuesday that its largest-ever crackdown on scammers has produced actions against more than 800 defendants since March, with cryptocurrency investment fraud run out of Southeast Asian scam centers among its top targets. The department announced the results of an anti-scam surge that followed President Donald Trump’s Executive Order 14390, signed March 6. Since then, prosecutors have acted in more than 400 cases, bringing new charges, extraditions, guilty verdicts and sentences across 85 federal districts. U.S. agents also helped police in more than 10 countries raid foreign scam call centers and compounds that targeted Americans. Thirty defendants were extradited to face charges in U.S. courts. “Predatory scams against the American people will not be tolerated,” Attorney General Todd Blanche said. “The unprecedented results of this surge are just the beginning.” More than $1 billion in crypto frozen Crypto sits at the center of much of the effort. The State Department said the U.S. and Southeast Asian law enforcement it funds and trains have helped freeze more than $1 billion in stolen cryptocurrency and take down more than 1.4 million fraudulent websites and accounts. The Justice Department’s Scam Center Strike Force, formed in 2025 to go after Southeast Asian crypto fraud, says its crypto seizure team has restrained about $1.08 billion in cryptocurrency from these schemes. The team is focused on returning stolen funds to victims. The FBI’s Operation Blackout has restrained nearly $17 billion in illicit funds, seized more than 14,000 digital devices and helped dismantle more than 29 scam compounds across Asia, Africa and the Middle East, the department said. The FBI also helped free and repatriate more than 2,200 trafficked workers forced to run scams inside those compounds. “The message to these scam syndicates is clear: if you target Americans, justice will find you,” FBI Director Kash Patel said. Scam cases tied to fake crypto platforms In the past month alone, the Criminal Division filed or unsealed charges against more than 30 scam defendants, including those tied to Southeast Asian scam centers running crypto investment fraud schemes. Other cases involved inheritance fraud, jury duty imposters working from Georgia prisons and sweepstakes schemes aimed at elderly Americans. The Secret Service said it has restrained more than $200 million in illicit funds during the surge. One of its cases identified a crypto investment conspiracy run from scam centers in Cambodia that targeted at least 174 U.S. victims. In October, a Chinese national was extradited from the Netherlands and arraigned in California over his alleged role. item.title: Pakistani astronaut becomes 1st international visitor to China's Tiangong space station (photos)
item.description: null For the first time ever, a foreign astronaut has set foot inside China's Tiangong space station. That pioneer is Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who arrived at Tiangong aboard the Shenzhou-24 spacecraft early this morning (Nov. 25). "The Chinese space station is always something to look forward to!" the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA) wrote in an update today (in Mandarin; translation by Google). "China's 'Tiangong' welcomes partners from all over the world to visit!" Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces, is a payload specialist on Shenzhou-24. He found his way onto the mission thanks to a space-cooperation agreement that China signed with Pakistan in Islamabad in February 2025 . Ali and his two Shenzhou-24 crewmates — commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi — enjoyed a short and smooth ride to their orbital destination. They lifted off atop a Long March 2F rocket on Tuesday (Nov. 24) at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT on Nov. 25) and reached Tiangong a little over six hours later. Tang and Wu will live aboard the outpost for the usual six-month stint. Ali, however, will come home in just a week, hitching a ride with two of the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who arrived at Tiangong in May . Ali will be busy during his short space stay, conducting a set of joint Chinese-Pakistani experiments. "Four collaborative projects in biotechnology and materials are planned, with Ali also scheduled to conduct an in-orbit experiment involving photosynthetic cyanobacteria," The Times of India wrote today . The third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will remain on the station until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore set a Chinese record, becoming the first astronaut from his country to live in low Earth orbit for a full year. Astronauts from the Soviet Union/Russia and the United States have already blazed this long-duration trail. The global record for longest continuous space stay is 437 days, set by cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov aboard the Mir space station from January 1994 to March 1995. Another look at the Shenzhou-23 and Shenzhou-24 astronauts aboard Tiangong on Nov. 25, 2026. (Image credit: CMSA) Ali is not the first person from Pakistan ever to reach space, by the way. That distinction belongs to adventurer Namira Salim, who traveled to suborbital space on a tourism flight with Virgin Galactic in October 2023. Shenzhou-24 is the 12th crewed mission to Tiangong, a three-module, T-shaped outpost that China finished assembling in late 2022. Well, "finished" might not be the right term; China plans to expand Tiangong , which is currently about 20% as massive as the International Space Station .

item.description: The Federal Government has flagged off the modernisation and upgrade of the Lagos Port Complex, Apapa, and Tin Can Island Port. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, supported by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, and other senior government officials, unveiled the project on Wednesday, describing it as a strategic investment that will reposition Nigeria as a leading maritime hub in Africa and strengthen the country’s competitiveness in global trade. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony at the Tin-Can Island Port, Oyetola said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits, reduce logistics costs, attract international shipping lines, stimulate industrial growth and create at least 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits (X/@GboyegaOyetola) He said the modernisation programme was a significant step towards realising President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises infrastructure development as a catalyst for economic growth, investment and job creation. According to the minister, the two ports, which have served as major gateways for Nigeria’s international commerce for decades, have become increasingly inadequate to meet the demands of a rapidly expanding economy and changing global shipping requirements. He noted that Apapa Port, established in 1913, was more than a century old, while Tin Can Island Port was commissioned in 1977 when Nigeria’s population stood at approximately 67.2 million, annual trade was about $17 billion, and cargo throughput was 8.11 million metric tonnes. Today, he said, Nigeria’s population has grown to approximately 240 million, merchandise trade exceeds $100 billion annually, while cargo throughput has increased to 129.3 million metric tonnes, nearly 16 times its 1977 level. Oyetola stressed that the mismatch between growing economic activities and ageing port infrastructure had made comprehensive modernisation both urgent and unavoidable. “The cost of inaction is far greater than the cost of modernisation,” he was quoted as saying in a statement by the special adviser to the minister, Bolaji Akinola, as saying, adding that Nigeria will not surrender its competitive advantage. “Our ambition is to attract more direct calls by international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo, expand transshipment opportunities and establish our ports as preferred gateways to trade across the African Continental Free Trade Area. We cannot achieve this ambition with infrastructure that falls behind the demands of modern shipping,” the minister said. item.title: Entertainment Week Africa 2026 Celebrates Five Years With a Week of Film, Music, Fashion, Tech and Art in Lagos
item.description: The fifth edition of Entertainment Week Africa brought together filmmakers, musicians, designers, artists, tech founders, investors, mentors, policymakers and fans for six days of screenings, showcases, masterclasses and celebrations under the theme Five Years of Closing the Gap . People from 121 countries and territories applied to speak, attend or screen their work, and more than 19,000 people joined the programme in person and online, as EWA streamed its sessions live for the first time. Over the six days, more than 150 speakers led nearly 100 panels, masterclasses, workshops, roundtables and podcast sessions, while around 50 films were screened across the week. The celebrations began on Opening Night at the Livespot Entertarium, where guests were treated to an evening of music, fashion, film and comedy to mark five years of EWA. Sixteen emerging artists performed in front of a room of industry leaders, creatives and partners, and the night featured an exclusive 30-minute screening of University of Side Hustle, the first scripted feature film from Livespot Studios , written by Dami Elebe and executive produced by Deola Art Alade . By day, EbonyLife Place hosted a packed programme across seven tracks: Film & TV; Music; Fashion & Beauty; AI & Tech; Art & Animation; Live Events & Production; and Creative Enterprise. Nissi Ogulu led a masterclass on animation as Africa’s next big storytelling frontier, and From Lagos to Disney explored what it takes to bring African stories to global screens. Creators picked up practical tips in sessions with Victoire, Ifeoma Udeme and Canva. Other sessions tackled sync licensing, music funding, building Africa’s touring circuit and turning creative skills into businesses. The podcast stage kept the energy going with live recordings of CreativiTea and Crea8torium , which closed the final day. Fashion took over the Entertarium for The Runway Coterie, an evening of bold collections that ended with the announcement of the EWA Fashion Lab winners after a week-long programme with mentors. Hooked By Lade won first place with ₦2 million, Estaz took second place and ₦1 million, and Melira placed third, winning ₦500,000. Lush Hair styled the runway as the show’s hair sponsor. Next door, the EWA Art Floor invited guests into The Spaces Between Us , an exhibition that blended photography, painting, installation, archival work, fashion and live performance. Curated by Jumoke Sanwo and produced with Revolving Art Incubator (RAI) as it celebrated its tenth anniversary, the exhibition featured work by 21 Nigerian artists and seven fashion designers. In the EWA Sound Lab, producers and songwriters spent time creating alongside Banx & Ranx, the Grammy-nominated, Juno Award-winning duo whose credits include records for Sean Paul, Dua Lipa and Ella Eyre . item.title: Ladybird browser's first downloadable alpha is surprisingly capable
item.description: Note: At the time of writing, I was unaware of criticism directed at Ladybird creator Andreas Kling’s public statements. Readers interested in this background can find further context in accounts by Kelson Vibber and Drew DeVault . After four years of work to build a browser engine from scratch, the Ladybird project released its first downloadable alpha on November 23, offering prebuilt versions for macOS and Linux. Previously, curious users had to compile the browser themselves from its source. Now it's an installable package with automatic updating. Ladybird is most notable for what it isn't: another browser fork. Where Chrome, Edge, Brave, and Opera all run on Google's Blink engine, and Firefox depends on Gecko, Ladybird's rendering engine and its LibJS JavaScript engine were written from scratch. "The engine is our own, built from the ground up, and not a fork," project lead Andreas Kling wrote in Monday's announcement. "The browser around it is modest, but functional."
