item.title: Tunji Olowolafe Wants Ikogosi to Be Nigeria’s Next Destination for Weddings, Retreats and Landmark Celebrations
item.description: Growing up, Tunji Olowolafe ’s parents brought the family to Are-Ekiti every Christmas, and a trip to Ikogosi was compulsory. Decades later, he returned to the warm springs town with family, friends and business partners, “not to take away, but to help build something enduring in Ekiti.” Speaking as Chairman and Chief Launcher of Ikogosi Day 2026, Thanksgiving and Launch of the Oba’s Palace Project, on Saturday, 14 November 2026, the Chancellor of Ekiti State University set out a vision for Ikogosi built on intentional tourism, enterprise and heritage. Dr. Olowolafe said Ikogosi’s task now is to give visitors compelling reasons to come, stay longer and spend across local businesses. He pointed to the recent Ikogosi 17.5km Race, which drew runners from across Nigeria alongside athletes from Ghana, Kenya and Ethiopia, as an example of what happens when private initiative meets local hospitality. He urged the same thinking for lifestyle and executive tourism, with the ambition of making Ikogosi a premier international destination for weddings, milestone birthdays, corporate retreats and landmark gatherings. “Our natural landscape will draw people in. But only the quality of the experience we deliver, through warmth of welcome, impeccable service and attention to detail, will bring them back,” he said. To build that service culture, he called for a deeper, structured partnership between the Ikogosi Resort and the Hospitality Management Technology Department of the Federal Polytechnic, Ado-Ekiti, which has already produced two sets of National Diploma graduates. The goal is for students to train alongside seasoned professionals while serving real guests. He also proposed alliances with leading international hospitality institutes to benchmark local teaching and service, noting that world-class hospitality must become Ekiti’s signature. He argued that the same commercial discipline must apply to the resources beneath the ground. “It is not enough to say we have clay or kaolin. We must ask: What are their exact industrial specifications? What can we competitively manufacture? And who is ready to buy?” he said. He tasked the Department of Geology at Ekiti State University, headed by Professor Yinka Aturamu , with establishing precise data on local deposits and mapping out what it would take to turn them into viable commercial enterprises. For him, the measure of success is what it changes for young people in the community. “For a young person growing up in Ikogosi, the result must be tangible: a marketable skill, a steady job, a supply contract or a thriving enterprise,” he said. He cited Rasheed Sarumi’s Saroafrica Group as proof of what is possible. The group acquired Gossy Warm Springs in 2018 and restored the plant to full production in 2019. Together with its partners, Saroafrica is now investing US$25 million in a manufacturing facility in Ikogosi, which will run on its own 2MW gas-fired power plant. item.title: Miss Universe 2026: Meet the 17 African Queens Representing the Continent
item.description: From left: Miss Universe Democratic Republic of the Congo 2026 Jessi Kalambayi, Miss Universe Namibia 2026 Charene Labuschagne, and Miss Universe Botswana 2026 Dabilo Moses ahead of the 75th Miss Universe finale in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The Miss Universe stage is getting a beautiful dose of African representation this year, with 17 contestants from across the continent making their way to Puerto Rico for the pageant’s 75th edition. And there are plenty of stories to discover among them, from Uganda ’s historic debut to Nigeria ’s Danielle Adewusi , whose journey to the competition comes with a lovely family connection. Taking place in San Juan, Puerto Rico, the Diamond Anniversary edition will bring together 116 contestants from around the world, all hoping to claim the newly unveiled 75th-anniversary crown, The Radiance of an Eternal Legacy. The grand finale is scheduled for Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at the José Miguel Agrelot Coliseum. This year’s show will be hosted by R’Bonney Gabriel , Mario Lopez , Zuri Hall and Dayanara Torres . At the end of the night, reigning Miss Universe 2025 Fátima Bosch of Mexico will pass on her crown to a new winner. Bosch took the title in Thailand last November, ahead of contestants from Thailand, Venezuela, the Philippines and Côte d’Ivoire. For Africa, the road to this year’s competition has come with a few changes. Angola, the Republic of the Congo, South Sudan, Zambia and Zimbabwe were unable to participate due to U.S. travel and visa restrictions, while Côte d’Ivoire, Mauritius, Rwanda and Senegal withdrew from the competition. Still, 17 African countries have contestants in the running, including Uganda, which is making its historic Miss Universe debut. Cameroon, Ethiopia, Kenya, Sierra Leone and Tunisia are among the countries returning to the global stage. Representing Nigeria is 29-year-old medical doctor and women’s health advocate Danielle Adewusi, also known as Danielle Fadeke Adewusi. Her participation adds a special family detail to the story: she won Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 in Lagos, 35 years after her mother, Tonia Okogbenin , represented the country at Miss Universe 1991. From first-time participation to familiar faces returning to the competition, these are the 17 African beauty queens representing the continent at Miss Universe 2026. Dabilo Moses — Botswana Representing Botswana is 26-year-old Dabilo Moses from Gaborone (born in Tutume). A Broadcasting and Journalism student at Limkokwing University of Creative Technology, she previously won Miss Independence Botswana 2022, reached the Top 24 at Miss Supranational 2023 as Botswana’s first-ever entrant, and was appointed Miss Universe Botswana 2026 after finishing as first runner-up in 2025. Miss Universe Botswana 2026 Dabilo Moses at the 75th Miss Universe competition in San Juan, Puerto Rico. item.title: Inside PluggedIN 2026: One of Africa’s Biggest Creator and Brand Summits by Woof Studios
item.description: The evolving business of content creation took centre stage in Lagos as Woof Studios Africa , in partnership with Insight Redefini , hosted the second edition of PluggedIN 2026 in Victoria Island, Lagos. The gathering brought together some of Nigeria’s leading content creators, filmmakers, advertising professionals and brand executives to explore how digital influence can translate into original intellectual property, sustainable creative businesses and longer-term commercial opportunities. Hosted by actress and media personality Bisola Aiyeola , the event gave creators a platform to present original concepts and explore new possibilities for collaboration with brands and industry stakeholders. From Content Creation to Intellectual Property A major highlight of PluggedIN 2026 was its creator showcase, featuring Taaooma, Layi Wasabi, Aproko Doctor, Ify’s Kitchen, Biodun Stephen, Osas Ighodaro, Shank Comics, Folagade Banks, Afropolitan, Bolaji Ogunmola, and Geena Foodies n Spice . The creators presented original ideas, show formats and potential collaborative projects, offering a glimpse into the range of stories and formats emerging from Nigeria’s creative community. The opportunity for brands lies in being part of that process through partnerships that go beyond individual sponsored posts to support the development, production and distribution of original content. For Adetutu Laditan , Creator Economy Catalyst and Founder of Woof Studios Africa, this shift requires a more structured approach to supporting creators and connecting them with the right opportunities. “Our vision at Woof Studios Africa has always been to empower African creators to move beyond virality and build lasting, profitable enterprises. Nigerian creators are thinking bigger, and forward-thinking brands want to be part of that evolution,” she said. Laditan explained that Woof Studios works across the business and production aspects of content development, including funding and distribution, to help creators take ideas beyond their initial digital formats. “When creators understand a brand’s business objectives, and brands respect the authentic voice a creator has spent years cultivating, we stop simply buying attention and start co-creating stories that matter.” The conversations at PluggedIN also addressed the realities of building sustainable creative businesses. During the creator-focused panel, Kiekie, Craze Clown, Jay On-Air and Winifred Nwania of Zeelicious Food discussed the opportunities and challenges of building careers in the digital space. They explored content ownership, audience engagement, monetisation and the importance of meaningful brand relationships. The discussions reflected an increasingly important question for the industry: How can creators turn the audiences and cultural influence they have built into sustainable businesses? item.description: The SpaceX Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft is seen as it lands with NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev aboard in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Los Angeles, Calif., Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026.

item.title: Artemis II Crew Moon Photo Annotations
item.description: A visualization of a dark Moon eclipsing the Sun is marked with handwritten notes in this April 6, 2026, screenshot from an Artemis II crew member's tablet.

item.title: NASA Astronaut Christina Koch at Eagles vs. Rams
item.description: NASA astronaut and mission specialist of the agency's Artemis II mission, Christina Koch, led the fans in singing the Eagles Fight Song from the field at an NFL game between the Philadelphia Eagles and the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026, in Philadelphia.

item.title: Apple iPhone 18 Pro review: big changes for small differences
item.description: Longer battery life, better screen, upgraded Siri and new variable aperture camera in refreshed design from last year’s model Apple’s smaller Pro iPhone gets the best kind of spec bump for 2026: longer battery life, faster chips and a fancy new variable aperture for the main camera. The iPhone 18 Pro is one of a pair of slab phones launched alongside Apple’s first folding phone , the iPhone Duo, and is the cheapest of the new phones, with a regular iPhone 18 yet to be announced. Screen: 6.3in Super Retina XDR (120Hz OLED) (460ppi) Processor: Apple A20 Pro RAM: 12GB Storage: 256GB, 512GB or 1TB Operating system: iOS 27 Camera: 48MP + 48MP UW + 48MP 4x, 18MP front-facing Connectivity: 5G, wifi 7, NFC, Bluetooth 6, Thread, USB-C, Satellite, UWB and GNSS Water resistance: IP68 (6 metres for 30 mins) Dimensions: 150 x 71.9 x 8.75mm Weight: 211g Continue reading...

item.title: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 Launches
item.description: A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket carrying the company's Dragon spacecraft is launched on NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station with NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov aboard, Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

item.title: Star Trails
item.description: This long-duration image shows star trails above Earth and the blue lights of fishing boats and the yellow lights of Indonesian cities stretching below the International Space Station as it orbited 258 miles above the Banda Sea.

item.title: Crew-13 Rocket and Spacecraft at Launch Pad
item.description: Ahead of launch of NASA’s SpaceX Crew-13 mission, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, with the Dragon spacecraft atop, is vertical at the launch pad of Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026.

item.title: NASA's Hubble Telescope Reaches Milestone, Looks for Elusive Supernova
item.description: An image from NASA's Hubble Space Telescope of galaxy cluster MACS J0417 is part of repeated observations to monitor for the reappearance of supernova Athena, which can help astronomers measure the expansion rate of the universe.

item.description: NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik (left) and ESA (European Space Agency) astronaut Luca Parmitano view progress on the solid rocket booster integration in High Bay 3 inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA's Kennedy Space Center in Florida on Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026.

item.title: Pixel 11 Pro Fold review: the foldable with the best triple camera
item.description: Big screen folder with slick software and advanced AI is just like a regular Android when closed Google’s latest folding phone sticks with its tried and tested design of a traditional phone shape when closed and almost square when open, in the face of new competition from Apple’s squat iPhone fold . The Pixel 11 Pro Fold is Google’s fourth-generation folder and is still one of the only models with a full water and dust resistance rating similar to standard slab phones. It costs from £1,799 (€1,999/$1,899/A$2,799), which is £50 (€100/$100/A$100) more than last year as the pressure of RAMageddon continues to push up prices. Continue reading...

item.title: NASA's Chandra Spots Galactic Gem
item.description: Galaxies are like cosmic gems, each with characteristics including size and shape that make them distinct. A gallery from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory and other telescopes displays a collection of galactic images that showcase this variety.

item.title: Superbubble in the Large Magellanic Cloud
item.description: N44 is a complex nebula filled with glowing hydrogen gas, dark lanes of dust, massive stars, and many populations of stars of different ages. One of its most distinctive features, however, is the dark, starry gap called a “superbubble,” visible in this Hubble Space Telescope image in the upper central region.

item.title: Lunar Occultation of Venus
item.description: On Wednesday, June 17, skywatchers across the United States—and parts of Canada—enjoyed a rare event: a daytime lunar occultation of Venus. A lunar occultation occurs when the Moon moves directly in front of another celestial object from our viewpoint on Earth, briefly hiding it from sight.

item.title: Igniting Roman's Journey
item.description: Now on a three-month, million-mile journey to its final orbit, NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will soon reveal the universe’s darkest secrets. The mission launched at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Aug. 30 aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket from Launch Complex 39A at the agency’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

item.title: August Lunar Eclipse Rises Over Louisiana
item.description: A lunar eclipse is visible over southern Louisiana. The lunar eclipse was visible throughout much of North and South America and part of Europe and Africa between Aug. 27-28. The Full Moon slipped through Earth’s shadow on Aug. 27, continuing into Aug. 28 for some parts of the world, resulting in the lunar eclipse. At maximum eclipse, the Moon takes on a dramatic dark, ruddy or coppery tint along the covered edge. New Orleans is home to NASA’s Michoud Assembly Facility, where stages for NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket and structures for Orion spacecraft are produced for the Artemis missions.

item.title: Artemis III RS-25 Engine Processing: #3 Lift
item.description: Technicians prepare to transfer the #2 RS-25 SLS (Space Launch System) rocket engine (front) to the work stand with the #3 engine (back) for integration with the Artemis III core stage rocket on Tuesday, Aug. 25, 2026, inside the Vehicle Assembly Building at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida. During Artemis III, the four RS‑25 engines will launch the Orion spacecraft and its crew of four into low Earth orbit, generating more than two million pounds of thrust at liftoff.

item.title: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
item.description: A SpaceX Falcon Heavy rocket with NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Telescope on board is seen transiting the sun during launch from Launch Complex 39A, Sunday, Aug. 30, 2026, at NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
